title.en: Volume 64 Biographies 54: Jiang Ziyi, Hu Sengyou, Xu Wencheng, Yin Zichun, Du Zewang, Lin Zhangbiao
title.raw: 卷六十四 列傳第五十四 江子一 胡僧祐 徐文盛 陰子春 杜崱 王琳 張彪 Volume 64 Biographies 54: Jiang Ziyi, Hu Sengyou, Xu Wencheng, Yin Zichun, Du Zewang, Lin Zhangbiao

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十四

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Four
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 54

sentences.zh: 江子一胡僧佑徐文盛陰子春杜崱王琳張彪

translations.literal: Jiang Ziyi, Hu Sengyou, Xu Wencheng, Yin Zichun, Du Qi, Wang Lin, Zhang Biao
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ziyi, Hu Sengyou, Xu Wencheng, Yin Zichun, Du Qi, Wang Lin, and Zhang Biao

sentences.zh: 江子一字元亮，濟陽考城人，晉散騎常侍統之七世孫也。

translations.literal: Jiang Ziyi, style name Yuanliang, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang, the seventh-generation descendant of Jin's Regular Attendant-at-Large Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ziyi, whose style name was Yuanliang, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang. He was the seventh-generation descendant of Jiang Tong, Regular Attendant-at-Large under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父法成，奉朝請。

translations.literal: His father Facheng was a Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiang Facheng held the post of Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences.

sentences.zh: 子一少慷慨有大志。

translations.literal: Ziyi in his youth was generous and high-minded, with great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ziyi was open-handed and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 家貧，以孝聞，苦侍養多闕；

translations.literal: His family was poor; he was known for filial piety, yet he suffered many lapses in attending to his parents' needs;
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor. He was famed for filial devotion, yet he often could not fully provide for his parents;

sentences.zh: 因終身蔬食。

translations.literal: therefore he ate only vegetables for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: and so he ate only plain vegetarian fare for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 仕梁起家為王國侍郎、奉朝請。

translations.literal: Entering service under Liang, he began as a Kingdom Attendant and Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Liang service as Kingdom Attendant and Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences.

sentences.zh: 上書言事，為當軸所排，乃拜表求入北為刺客。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on state affairs, was pushed aside by those in power, and then memorialized requesting to go north as an assassin.
translations.idiomatic: After a memorial on public affairs earned him the enmity of those at the helm, he petitioned to be sent north as an assassin.

sentences.zh: 武帝異之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu regarded this as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was struck by his daring.

sentences.zh: 又啟求觀書秘閣，武帝許之，有敕直華林省。

translations.literal: He also petitioned to read books in the Secret Archive; Emperor Wu granted it, and an edict assigned him duty at the Hualin Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked leave to read in the Secret Archive. The emperor agreed and ordered him stationed at the Hualin Office.

sentences.zh: 其姑夫左衛將軍朱異權要當朝，休下之日，賓客輻湊。

translations.literal: His uncle by marriage, Left Guards General Zhu Yi, held power at court; on his days off, guests converged in crowds.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle by marriage Zhu Yi, Left Guards General, was the man of the hour. On his days off guests thronged his gate.

sentences.zh: 異不為物議所歸，欲引子一為助，子一未嘗造門，其高潔如此。

translations.literal: Yi was not approved in public opinion and wished to draw Ziyi to his aid, but Ziyi never once called at his door—such was his lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi lacked public esteem and sought Ziyi's backing, but Ziyi never once crossed his threshold—so upright was he.

sentences.zh: 為遂昌、曲阿令，皆著美績。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Suichang and Qu'e, in both posts he left distinguished records.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Suichang and then Qu'e he earned a reputation for excellent administration.

sentences.zh: 後為南津校尉。

translations.literal: Later he became Commandant of Southern Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Commandant of Southern Ford.

sentences.zh: 弟子四，曆尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zisi had served as Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue's Gold Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zisi had served as Gentleman of the Gold Bureau in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大同初，遷右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Datong era he was promoted to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 兄弟性並剛烈。

translations.literal: The brothers were alike in fierce, unyielding temper.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers shared a fierce, unyielding temper.

sentences.zh: 子四自右丞上封事，極言得失，武帝甚善之，詔曰：「屋漏在上，知之在下，其令尚書詳擇，施于時政。」

translations.literal: From his post as Right Vice Director, Zisi submitted a sealed memorial setting forth gains and losses in the utmost detail. Emperor Wu greatly approved it and issued an edict: "When the roof leaks, those above know it through those below—let the Ministry of State Affairs examine this carefully and apply it to current policy.
translations.idiomatic: From the Right Vice Directorship Zisi submitted a sealed memorial on what was right and wrong in government. Emperor Wu praised it highly and decreed: "When the roof leaks, those above learn of it from those below. Let the Ministry of State Affairs review this carefully and put what fits into practice.

sentences.zh: 左戶郎沈炯、少府丞顧璵嘗奏事不允，帝厲色呵責之。

translations.literal: Left Household Gentleman Shen Jiong and Junior Chamberlain Gu Yu once reported on affairs without gaining approval; the emperor rebuked them sternly with a harsh countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Household Gentleman Shen Jiong and Junior Chamberlain Gu Yu once failed to win approval on a report, the emperor scolded them harshly to their faces.

sentences.zh: 子四乃趨前代炯等對，對甚激切。

translations.literal: Zisi then hurried forward to answer in place of Jiong and the others; his reply was exceedingly sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Zisi stepped forward to answer for Jiong and the others in words that cut deep.

sentences.zh: 帝怒呼縛之，子四乃據地不受。

translations.literal: In anger the emperor ordered him bound, but Zisi sat on the ground and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in fury ordered him bound. Zisi sat down on the ground and refused to be taken.

sentences.zh: 帝怒亦歇，乃釋之，猶坐免職。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger also subsided, and he released him, yet Zisi was still punished by dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath cooled and he let him go, but Zisi was still removed from office.

sentences.zh: 及侯景攻陷曆陽，自橫江將度，子一帥舟師千餘人於下流欲邀之，其副董桃生走，子一乃退還南洲，收余眾步赴建鄴，見於文德殿。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing captured Liyang and was about to cross from Hengjiang, Ziyi led more than a thousand men in river craft downstream intending to intercept him. His deputy Dong Taosheng fled; Ziyi then withdrew to South Islet, gathered the remaining troops, marched to Jiankang, and was received at Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took Liyang and prepared to cross the Yangzi from Hengjiang, Ziyi led a fleet of more than a thousand men downstream to intercept him. His deputy Dong Taosheng deserted. Ziyi fell back to South Islet, rallied what forces remained, marched overland to Jiankang, and was received in Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝怒之，具以事對，且曰：「臣以身許國，常恐不得其死，今日之事，何所復惜。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry with him. He reported the whole affair and said: "Your servant has pledged his body to the state and always feared he might not die as he ought. In today's matter, what is there left to spare?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Ziyi gave a full account and said: "I have pledged my life to the state and always feared I might not die as a loyal man should. In what happened today, what is there left for me to hold back?

sentences.zh: 不死闕前，終死闕後耳。」

translations.literal: If I do not die before the palace gates, in the end I shall die behind them.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not die before the palace gates, I shall die behind them in the end.

sentences.zh: 及城被圍，開承明門出戰。

translations.literal: When the city was besieged, Chenming Gate was opened and they went out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was besieged, Chenming Gate was opened and they sallied forth to battle.

sentences.zh: 子一及弟尚書左丞子四、東宮直殿主帥子五並力戰直前，賊坐甲不起。

translations.literal: Ziyi, together with his brothers—the Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Zisi and the Eastern Palace Direct-Hall Commander Ziwu—fought forward with all their strength. The rebels sat in armor and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi, his brother Zisi the Left Vice Director, and his brother Ziwu commander of the Eastern Palace guard fought straight ahead with all their might. The rebels sat armored and would not stand.

sentences.zh: 子一引矟撞之，賊縱突騎，眾並縮。

translations.literal: Ziyi charged with his spear and struck them; the rebels loosed their shock cavalry, and all shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi drove in with his spear. The rebels unleashed shock cavalry and everyone fell back.

sentences.zh: 子一刺其騎，騎倒矟折，賊解其肩，時年六十二。

translations.literal: Ziyi stabbed one of their horsemen; the horseman fell and the spear broke. The rebels dismembered his shoulder. He was sixty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He ran a rider through; the man fell and Ziyi's spear snapped. The rebels cut off his shoulder. He was sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 弟曰：「與兄俱出，何面獨旋。」

translations.literal: A brother said: "We went out together with our elder brother—what face have we to return alone?
translations.idiomatic: One brother cried: "We marched out with our elder brother—how can we turn back alone?

sentences.zh: 乃免胄赴敵，子四矟洞胸死，子五傷脰，還至塹一慟而絕。

translations.literal: They doffed their helmets and rushed at the enemy. Zisi died with a spear through his chest; Ziwu was wounded in the neck, returned to the moat, gave one great cry of grief, and expired.
translations.idiomatic: They tore off their helmets and charged the enemy. Zisi took a spear through the chest and died. Ziwu was struck in the neck, reached the moat, gave one great sob, and died.

sentences.zh: 賊義子一之勇，歸之，面如生。

translations.literal: The rebels admired Ziyi's valor, returned his body, and his face was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels respected Ziyi's courage, returned his body, and his face looked as though he still lived.

sentences.zh: 詔贈子一給事黃門侍郎，子四中書侍郎，子五散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded Ziyi the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; Zisi, Vice Director of the Secretariat; Ziwu, Attendant Cavalry Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted Ziyi Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Zisi Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Ziwu Attendant Cavalry Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，元帝又追贈子一侍中，諡義子；

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan further posthumously granted Ziyi the post of Palace Attendant, posthumous title Yizi;
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was crushed, Emperor Yuan further granted Ziyi the post of Palace Attendant with the posthumous title Loyal Son;

sentences.zh: 子四黃門侍郎，諡毅子；

translations.literal: Zisi, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, posthumous title Yizi;
translations.idiomatic: Zisi Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, posthumous title Resolute Son;

sentences.zh: 子五中書侍郎，諡烈子。

translations.literal: Ziwu, Vice Director of the Secretariat, posthumous title Liezi.
translations.idiomatic: Ziwu Vice Director of the Secretariat, posthumous title Fierce Son.

sentences.zh: 子一續黃圖及班固「九品」，並辭賦文章數十篇，行於世。

translations.literal: Ziyi continued the Yellow Chart and Ban Gu's "Nine Ranks," as well as several tens of rhapsodies, fu, and essays, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi continued the Yellow Chart and Ban Gu's Nine Ranks, and left several dozen fu, rhapsodies, and essays still in circulation.

sentences.zh: 晚事梁元帝。

translations.literal: In his later years he served Emperor Yuan of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he served Emperor Yuan of Liang.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，西沮蠻反，元帝令僧佑討之，使盡誅其渠帥。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of Hou Jing, the Western Ju tribes rebelled. Emperor Yuan ordered Sengyou to suppress them and commanded that all their chieftains be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion the Western Ju tribes rose. Emperor Yuan sent Sengyou against them with orders to execute every chieftain.

sentences.zh: 僧佑諫忤旨，下獄。

translations.literal: Sengyou remonstrated against the imperial will and was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou remonstrated against the order, offended the throne, and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 大寶二年，景圍王僧辯于巴陵，元帝乃引僧佑於獄，拜為假節、武猛將軍，封新市縣侯，令援僧辯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dabao, Jing besieged Wang Sengbian at Baling. Emperor Yuan then brought Sengyou out of prison, appointed him Acting Commissioner with Credentials and Fierce Martial General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xinshi County, and ordered him to rescue Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dabao, Hou Jing besieged Wang Sengbian at Baling. Emperor Yuan released Sengyou from prison, made him Acting Commissioner with Credentials and Fierce Martial General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xinshi, and ordered him to relieve Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 將發泣下，謂其子屺曰：「汝可開朱白二門，吾不捷則死。

translations.literal: As he was about to set out he wept and said to his son Qi: "You may open the red and white gates. If I do not win, then I die.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to march he wept and told his son Qi: "Open the red gate if I win and the white gate if I lose. If I do not prevail, I die.

sentences.zh: 吉則由朱，凶則由白也。」

translations.literal: If auspicious, then by the red; if inauspicious, then by the white.
translations.idiomatic: Victory comes through the red; defeat through the white.

sentences.zh: 元帝聞而壯之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan heard of this and admired his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan heard this and admired his resolve.

sentences.zh: 前至赤沙亭，會陸法和至，乃與並軍，大敗景將任約軍，禽約送江陵。

translations.literal: Advancing to Chisha Pavilion, he met Lu Fahe arriving, joined forces, and utterly defeated Hou Jing's general Ren Yue's army, captured Yue, and sent him to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Chisha Pavilion, joined Lu Fahe, and together they routed the army of Hou Jing's general Ren Yue, captured Yue, and sent him to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 侯景聞之遂遁。

translations.literal: Hou Jing heard of this and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing heard the news and fled.

sentences.zh: 後拜領軍將軍，厚自封殖。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Palace Guards and enriched himself heavily.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General of the Palace Guards and amassed great private wealth.

sentences.zh: 以所加鼓吹恒置齋中，對之自娛。

translations.literal: He always kept the added drum-and-pipe music in his study and amused himself facing it.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the ceremonial drum-and-pipe band he had been granted permanently in his study and entertained himself before it.

sentences.zh: 人曰：「此是羽儀，公名望隆重，不宜若此。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "This is regalia of state. Your Lordship's fame and standing are weighty; it is not fitting to do thus.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told him: "That music is state regalia. A man of your standing ought not behave so.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「我性愛之，恒須見耳。」

translations.literal: He answered: "By nature I love it and must always see it."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I love it by nature and must always have it before my eyes."

sentences.zh: 或出遊亦以自隨，人士笑之。

translations.literal: When he went out on excursions he also took it with him, and gentlemen laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: When he traveled abroad he took the band with him as well, and people laughed.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he became General of Chariots and Cavalry with Bountiful Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengsheng he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with Bountiful Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 及魏軍至，以僧佑為都督城東諸軍事。

translations.literal: When the Wei army arrived, Sengyou was made Commander of all military affairs east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei army arrived he was made commander of all forces east of the city.

sentences.zh: 俄中流矢卒，城遂潰。

translations.literal: Soon he was struck by a stray arrow and died; the city then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was struck by a stray arrow and died, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 徐文盛字道茂，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Xu Wencheng, style name Daomao, was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wencheng, style name Daomao, was from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 家本魏將。

translations.literal: His family had originally been Wei generals.
translations.idiomatic: His family had originally served as Wei generals.

sentences.zh: 父慶之，梁天監初自北歸南，未至道卒。

translations.literal: His father Qingzhi, at the beginning of Liang's Tianjian era, returned from the north to the south but died on the road before arriving.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingzhi set out from the north for the south early in the Tianjian era but died on the road before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 文盛仍統其眾，稍立功績。

translations.literal: Wencheng still commanded his father's troops and gradually achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng took command of his father's men and gradually won distinction.

sentences.zh: 大同末，為甯州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong he became Inspector of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Datong era he became Inspector of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州在僻遠，群蠻劫竊相尋，前後刺史莫能制。

translations.literal: The province lay in a remote corner; tribal bands plundered in succession, and successive inspectors had been unable to control them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay in a remote corner where tribal raiders struck again and again, and no previous inspector had been able to control them.

sentences.zh: 文盛推心撫慰，夷人感之，風俗遂改。

translations.literal: Wencheng treated them with open heart and comfort; the tribes were moved, and customs thereupon changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng won them with sincerity and kindness. The tribes were moved, and local customs changed.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，聞國難，乃召募得數萬人來赴，元帝以為秦州刺史，加都督，授以東討之略。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, hearing of the national crisis, he recruited several tens of thousands of men and came to answer the call. Emperor Yuan made him Inspector of Qinzhou with added status as Commander and entrusted him with the strategy for the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing, hearing of the national crisis, he raised tens of thousands of men and marched east. Emperor Yuan made him Inspector of Qin Prefecture with command authority and entrusted him with the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 東下至武昌，遇侯景將任約，遂與相持。

translations.literal: He went east downriver to Wuchang, encountered Hou Jing's general Ren Yue, and thereupon locked in stalemate with him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched downriver to Wuchang, met Hou Jing's general Ren Yue, and settled into a stalemate.

sentences.zh: 元帝又命護軍將軍尹悅、平東將軍杜幼安、巴州刺史王珣等會之，並受文盛節度。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan also ordered Protector of the Army Yin Yue, Pacifier of the East Du You'an, Inspector of Bazhou Wang Xun, and others to join him, all placed under Wencheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan also ordered Protector of the Army Yin Yue, Pacifier of the East Du You'an, Inspector of Ba Prefecture Wang Xun, and others to join him, all under Wencheng's command.

sentences.zh: 大敗約于貝磯。

translations.literal: He utterly defeated Yue at Beiji.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Yue at Beiji.

sentences.zh: 約退保西陽，文盛進據蘆洲，又與相持。

translations.literal: Yue withdrew to defend Xiyang; Wencheng advanced and seized Luzhou, and again they faced each other in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Yue fell back to Xiyang. Wencheng advanced to Luzhou and again the two armies faced each other.

sentences.zh: 景聞之，率大眾西上援約，至西陽。

translations.literal: Jing heard of this, led a great host west upriver to relieve Yue, and reached Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing heard the news, led a great force upriver to relieve Yue, and reached Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸曰：「景水軍輕進，又甚饑疲，擊之必大捷。」

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Jing's river force has advanced lightly and is moreover very hungry and weary; if we strike, we are sure of a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said: "Jing's fleet has advanced recklessly and his men are starving and exhausted. Strike now and the victory will be complete.

sentences.zh: 文盛不許。

translations.literal: Wencheng would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng refused.

sentences.zh: 文盛妻石氏先在建鄴，至是，景載以還之。

translations.literal: Wencheng's wife, the Lady Shi, had earlier been in Jiankang; at this time Jing sent her back to him under escort.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng's wife Lady Shi had been in Jiankang. Now Hou Jing sent her back to him under escort.

sentences.zh: 文盛深德景，遂密通信使，都無戰心，眾咸憤怨。

translations.literal: Wencheng was deeply obliged to Jing and thereupon secretly exchanged messages with him; he had no will to fight at all, and the troops were all angry and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng felt deep gratitude toward Hou Jing and began secret correspondence with him. He lost all will to fight, and his troops seethed with anger.

sentences.zh: 杜幼安、宋簉等乃率所領獨進，大破景，獲其舟艦以歸。

translations.literal: Du You'an, Song Chou, and others then led their own troops forward alone, utterly defeated Jing, and returned with his ships.
translations.idiomatic: Du You'an, Song Chou, and others led their own troops forward on their own, routed Hou Jing, and returned with his ships.

sentences.zh: 會景密遣騎間道襲陷郢州，軍中懼，遂大潰，文盛奔還荊州。

translations.literal: Just then Jing secretly sent cavalry by a hidden route to strike and capture Yingzhou; the army was afraid and thereupon collapsed in great rout. Wencheng fled back to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Hou Jing sent cavalry by a hidden route and seized Ying Prefecture. Panic spread through the army, the host broke, and Wencheng fled back to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元帝仍以為城北面大都督，又聚斂贓汙甚多，元帝大怒，下令數其十罪，除其官爵。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan still made him Grand Commander of the north face of the city, but he also amassed much illicit wealth through exactions. Emperor Yuan was greatly angered, issued an order enumerating his ten crimes, and stripped him of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan still made him Grand Commander of the northern sector of the city, but Wencheng had also extorted vast illicit wealth. The emperor in fury listed ten crimes and stripped him of rank and office.

sentences.zh: 文盛私懷怨望，帝聞之，乃以下獄。

translations.literal: Wencheng privately harbored resentment; when the emperor heard of it, he was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng nursed private resentment. When the emperor heard of it, he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 時任約被禽，與文盛同禁。

translations.literal: At that time Ren Yue had been captured and was imprisoned together with Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue had just been captured and was imprisoned with him.

sentences.zh: 文盛謂約曰：「何不早降，令我至此。」

translations.literal: Wencheng said to Yue: "Why did you not surrender early and bring me to this pass?
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng said to Yue: "Why did you not surrender sooner and spare me this?

sentences.zh: 約曰：「門外不見卿馬跡，使我何處得降。」

translations.literal: Yue said: "Outside the gate one does not see your Lordship's horse tracks—where was I to surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied: "There were no tracks of your horses outside the gate. Where was I supposed to surrender?"

sentences.zh: 文盛無以答，遂死獄中。

translations.literal: Wencheng had nothing to answer and thereupon died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng had no reply and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 陰子春字幼文，武威姑臧人也。

translations.literal: Yin Zichun, style name Youwen, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zichun, style name Youwen, came from Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 晉義熙末，曾祖襲隨宋武帝南遷，至南平，因家焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin's Yixi era, his great-grandfather Xi followed Emperor Wu of Song in migrating south; reaching Nanping, the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yixi era his great-grandfather Xi followed Emperor Wu of Song south. The family settled at Nanping.

sentences.zh: 父智伯與梁武帝鄰居，少相善，嘗入帝臥內，見有異光成五色，因握帝手曰：「公後必大貴，非人臣也。

translations.literal: His father Zhibo was a neighbor of Emperor Wu of Liang; from youth they were on good terms. He once entered the emperor's sleeping quarters and saw a strange light forming five colors. Thereupon he grasped the emperor's hand and said: "Your Lordship will surely attain great eminence and is not fit to remain a subject.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhibo had been a neighbor of Emperor Wu of Liang and had known him from youth. Once he entered the emperor's bedchamber and saw a strange light in five colors. He took the emperor's hand and said: "You are destined for the highest fortune. You are not meant to remain a subject.

sentences.zh: 天下方亂，安蒼生者其在君乎。」

translations.literal: The realm is in turmoil; perhaps it is upon Your Lordship to bring peace to the living.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in turmoil. Perhaps you are the one to bring peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「幸勿多言。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Pray speak no more of this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Please say no more of this."

sentences.zh: 於是情好轉密，帝每有求，如外府焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon their affection grew closer; whenever the emperor had a request, it was as though to an external commandery.
translations.idiomatic: From then on their bond grew intimate. Whenever the emperor needed anything, Zhibo supplied it as freely as an external prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐阼，官至梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he reached the posts of Inspector of Liangzhou and Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Zhibo rose to Inspector of Liang and Qin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 子春仕歷位朐山戍主、東莞太守。

translations.literal: Zichun in office successively held the posts of Garrison Commander of Gushan and Administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zichun served as Garrison Commander of Gushan and then Administrator of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 時青州石鹿山臨海，先有神廟，刺史王神念以百姓祈禱糜費，毀神影，壞屋舍。

translations.literal: At that time on Shilu Mountain in Qingzhou, facing the sea, there had long been a spirit shrine. Inspector Wang Shennian, because the people's prayers wasted resources, destroyed the spirit image and demolished the buildings.
translations.idiomatic: On Shilu Mountain in Qingzhou, by the sea, there stood an old spirit shrine. Inspector Wang Shennian, deeming the people's offerings wasteful, destroyed the spirit image and tore down the buildings.

sentences.zh: 當坐棟上有一大蛇長丈餘，役夫打撲不禽，得入海水。

translations.literal: Just as they were seated on the ridge beam, a great serpent more than a zhang long appeared; laborers struck at it but could not capture it, and it entered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: As workmen sat on the ridge beam a serpent more than ten feet long appeared. They struck at it but could not catch it, and it slipped into the sea.

sentences.zh: 爾夜，子春夢見人通名詣子春云：「有人見苦，破壞宅舍。

translations.literal: That night Zichun dreamed of a man announcing his name who came to Zichun and said: "Someone has suffered hardship; his dwelling has been destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zichun dreamed that a man announced himself and came to him saying: "Someone has been wronged and his dwelling destroyed.

sentences.zh: 既無所托，欽君厚德，欲憩此境。」

translations.literal: Having nowhere to lodge, he admires your Lordship's deep virtue and wishes to rest in this region.
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere left to lodge, he admires your virtue and wishes to rest in your jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 子春心密記之。

translations.literal: Zichun secretly kept this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Zichun kept the dream in mind.

sentences.zh: 經二日而知之，甚驚，以為前所夢神。

translations.literal: After two days he learned of it and was greatly startled, thinking it was the spirit of his earlier dream.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he learned what had happened and was startled, believing it was the spirit of his dream.

sentences.zh: 因辦牲醑請召，安置一處。

translations.literal: He thereupon prepared sacrificial offerings and wine, invited the spirit, and settled it in one place.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared offerings and wine, summoned the spirit, and gave it a place to dwell.

sentences.zh: 數日，復夢一朱衣人相聞，辭謝云：「得君厚惠，當以一州相報。」

translations.literal: Several days later he again dreamed of a man in red garments who conveyed word and gave thanks, saying: "Having received your Lordship's generous kindness, I shall repay you with a whole province.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he dreamed again of a man in red robes who thanked him and said: "Having received your kindness, I shall repay you with a whole province.

sentences.zh: 子春心喜，供事彌勤。

translations.literal: Zichun was delighted in heart and served the spirit all the more diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Zichun was delighted and served the spirit all the more diligently.

sentences.zh: 經月余，魏欲襲朐山，間諜前知，子春設伏摧破之，詔授南青州刺史，鎮朐山。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Wei intended to strike Gushan; spies learned of it beforehand. Zichun set an ambush and crushed them. An edict appointed him Inspector of Southern Qingzhou, garrisoning Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later Wei planned an attack on Gushan. Spies brought word in advance. Zichun laid an ambush and crushed the enemy. An edict made him Inspector of Southern Qing Prefecture with his seat at Gushan.

sentences.zh: 又遷都督、梁秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was further transferred to Commander and Inspector of Liangzhou and Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Commander and Inspector of Liang and Qin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 子春雖無佗才行，臨人以廉潔稱。

translations.literal: Although Zichun had no other ability or conduct to speak of, in governing people he was known for integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Zichun had little else to recommend him, but as a magistrate he was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 閨門混雜，而身服垢汙，腳數年一洗，言每洗則失財敗事，雲在梁州，以洗足致梁州敗。

translations.literal: His inner quarters were disorderly, yet his person wore filth; he washed his feet only once every several years, saying that each washing brought loss of wealth and ruin of affairs. It was said that in Liangzhou, washing his feet had led to Liangzhou's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: His household was disorderly, yet he himself went filthy. He washed his feet only once every few years, saying each wash brought loss and ruin. People said that in Liang Prefecture he had lost the province because he washed his feet.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，徵為左衛將軍，遷侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was summoned as Left Guards General and promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing he was summoned as Left Guards General and promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景亂，元帝令子春隨王僧辯攻平邵陵王。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan ordered Zichun to follow Wang Sengbian in attacking and pacifying the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan ordered Zichun to follow Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 又與左衛將軍徐文盛東討景，至貝磯與景遇，子春力戰，恒冠諸軍。

translations.literal: He also joined Left Guards General Xu Wencheng in the eastern campaign against Jing; reaching Beiji they encountered Jing's forces. Zichun fought fiercely and always led the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He also marched east with Left Guards General Xu Wencheng against Hou Jing. At Beiji they met the enemy, and Zichun fought so fiercely that he always led the field.

sentences.zh: 會郢州陷沒，軍遂退，卒於江陵。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou fell, the army withdrew and he died at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying Prefecture fell the army retreated, and he died at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 子鏗。

translations.literal: His son Keng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yin Keng.

sentences.zh: 鏗字子堅，博涉史傳，尤善五言詩，被當時所重。

translations.literal: Keng, style name Zijian, was broadly versed in histories and biographies and especially skilled in five-character verse; he was esteemed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Keng, style name Zijian, was widely read in history and biography and especially gifted in five-character verse. His contemporaries held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 為梁湘東王法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Aide in the Law Section under the Prince of Xiangdong of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Aide in the Law Section under the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 初鏗嘗與賓友宴飲，見行觴者，因回酒炙以授之，眾坐皆笑。

translations.literal: Early on, at a feast with guests and friends, Keng saw the cup-bearer passing and turned back wine and meat to hand to him; all seated laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast with friends he saw the cup-bearer pass and turned back wine and meat to give him. Everyone at the table laughed.

sentences.zh: 鏗曰：「吾儕終日酣酒，而執爵者不知其味，非人情也。」

translations.literal: Keng said: "We spend the whole day deep in wine, yet the one who holds the cup does not know its taste—this is not human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Keng said: "We drink all day, yet the man who holds the cup never tastes the wine. That is not how human beings should behave.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，鏗嘗為賊禽，或救之獲免。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Keng was once captured by bandits; someone rescued him and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Keng was once captured by the rebels. Someone rescued him and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 鏗問之，乃前所行觴者。

translations.literal: Keng asked who it was—it turned out to be the cup-bearer of former days.
translations.idiomatic: When Keng asked who had saved him, it was the cup-bearer from that feast.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，為始興王中錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In Chen's Tiankang era he became Central Recorder Aide under the Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen, in the Tiankang era, he became Central Recorder Aide to the Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗宴群臣賦詩，徐陵言之，帝即日召鏗預宴，使賦新成安樂宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once feasted the ministers and had them compose verse; Xu Ling spoke of him, and the emperor that same day summoned Keng to the feast and had him compose on the newly completed Palace of Peace and Joy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once held a feast for his ministers and ordered them to compose verse. Xu Ling spoke of Keng, and the emperor summoned him that same day and had him compose on the newly built Palace of Peace and Joy.

sentences.zh: 鏗援筆便就，帝甚歎賞之。

translations.literal: Keng took up the brush and finished at once; the emperor greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Keng took up his brush and finished at once. The emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 累遷晉陵太守，員外散騎常侍，頃之卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Administrator of Jinling and Supernumerary Attendant Cavalry Regular, and soon after died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Jinling and Supernumerary Attendant Cavalry Regular, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 有文集三卷行於世。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in three scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collected works in three scrolls circulated after his death.

sentences.zh: 杜崱，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Qi was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qi came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 其先自北歸南，居於雍州之襄陽，子孫因家焉，父懷寶少有志節，梁天監中累有軍功，後又立功南鄭，位梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: His ancestors had returned from the north to the south and settled at Xiangyang in Yongzhou; later generations made their home there. His father Huaibao in youth had will and integrity; in Liang's Tianjian era he repeatedly achieved military merit, later won merit again at Nanzheng, and reached the posts of Inspector of Liangzhou and Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had come south from the north and settled at Xiangyang in Yong Prefecture, where the family remained. His father Huaibao was ambitious from youth. Under Liang he won repeated military honors, later distinguished himself at Nanzheng, and rose to Inspector of Liang and Qin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大同初，魏軍復圍南鄭，懷寶命第三子嶷帥二百人與魏前鋒戰于光道寺，流矢中其目，失馬，敵人交矟將至，嶷斬其一騎而上，馳以歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, Wei armies again besieged Nanzheng. Huaibao ordered his third son Niao to lead two hundred men against the Wei vanguard at Guangdao Temple. A stray arrow struck his eye; he lost his horse; enemy spears crossed about to reach him. Niao cut down one rider and mounted, then galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong Wei forces again besieged Nanzheng. Huaibao sent his third son Niao with two hundred men against the Wei vanguard at Guangdao Temple. A stray arrow struck Niao's eye and he lost his horse as enemy spears closed in. He cut down a rider, mounted, and galloped back.

sentences.zh: 嶷膂力絕人，便馬善射，一日中戰七八合。

translations.literal: Niao's physical strength was unmatched among men; he was skilled on horseback and at archery and fought seven or eight engagements in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Niao's strength was unmatched. He was a superb horseman and archer and fought seven or eight battles in a single day.

sentences.zh: 所佩霜明朱弓四石餘力，斑絲纏矟長二丈五，同心敢死士百七十人。

translations.literal: The Frost-Bright red bow he carried drew more than four stone of force; his patterned-silk-wrapped spear was two zhang and five long; with him were one hundred seventy sworn death-defying warriors.
translations.idiomatic: He carried a red bow called Frost-Bright that drew more than four stone, and a silk-wrapped spear two and a half zhang long. One hundred seventy sworn warriors followed him.

sentences.zh: 每出殺傷數百人，敵人憚之，號為杜彪。

translations.literal: Each time he went out he killed and wounded several hundred men; the enemy feared him and called him Du Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Each sortie left hundreds dead or wounded. The enemy feared him and called him Du the Tiger.

sentences.zh: 懷寶卒於州，諡曰桓侯。

translations.literal: Huaibao died in the province; his posthumous title was Marquis Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Huaibao died in office and was posthumously titled Marquis Huan.

sentences.zh: 嶷位西荊州刺史，時讖言：「獨梁之下有瞎天子」，元帝以嶷其人也。

translations.literal: Niao held the post of Inspector of Western Jingzhou. At that time a prophecy read: "Beneath the character for 'alone' in Liang there is a blind Son of Heaven." Emperor Yuan thought Niao was that man.
translations.idiomatic: Niao became Inspector of Western Jing Prefecture. A prophecy then ran: "Beneath the character for 'alone' in Liang stands a blind Son of Heaven." Emperor Yuan believed Niao was meant.

sentences.zh: 會嶷改葬父祖，帝敕圖墓者惡為之，逾年而嶷卒。

translations.literal: When Niao reburied his father and grandfather, the emperor ordered the tomb-map makers to depict it ill; within a year Niao died.
translations.idiomatic: When Niao reburied his father and grandfather, the emperor ordered the tomb painters to portray the site unfavorably. Within a year Niao was dead.

sentences.zh: 崱，嶷弟也。

translations.literal: Qi was Niao's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was Niao's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 幼有志氣，居鄉里以膽勇稱，後為新興太守。

translations.literal: From youth he had spirit and resolve; in his home district he was known for courage, and later became Administrator of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was spirited and bold. In his home district he was famed for courage, and he later became Administrator of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，隨岳陽王來襲荊州，元帝與崱兄岸有舊，密書邀之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing he followed the Prince of Yueyang in coming to strike Jingzhou. Emperor Yuan had old ties with Qi's elder brother An and sent a secret letter inviting him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing he followed the Prince of Yueyang in an attack on Jingzhou. Emperor Yuan, who had old ties with Qi's brother An, sent a secret invitation.

sentences.zh: 崱乃與岸、弟幼安、兄子龕等夜歸元帝，以為武州刺史，封枝江縣侯，令隨領軍王僧辯東討侯景。

translations.literal: Qi thereupon joined An, his younger brother You'an, his elder brother's son Kan, and others in returning to Emperor Yuan by night. He was made Inspector of Wuzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang County, and ordered to follow the Commander of the Army Wang Sengbian in the eastern campaign against Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi joined An, his brother You'an, his nephew Kan, and others in returning to Emperor Yuan by night. He was made Inspector of Wu Prefecture, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang, and ordered to follow Wang Sengbian east against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 至巴陵，景遁。

translations.literal: Reaching Baling, Jing fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Baling Hou Jing fled.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，進爵為公，仍隨僧辯追景至石頭。

translations.literal: He was given the added post of Palace Attendant, advanced in rank to duke, and still followed Sengbian in pursuing Jing to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant and advanced to duke, then followed Sengbian in pursuit to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 景敗，崱入據台城。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated, Qi entered and seized Taicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was beaten, Qi entered and held Taicheng.

sentences.zh: 景平，加散騎常侍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: After Jing was pacified, he was given the added posts of Attendant Cavalry Regular and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was crushed he was made Attendant Cavalry Regular and Inspector of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是月，齊將郭元建攻秦州刺史嚴超達于秦郡，王僧辯令崱赴援，陳武帝亦自歐陽來會。

translations.literal: That month, Qi general Guo Yuanjian attacked Inspector of Qinzhou Yan Chaoda at Qin Commandery. Wang Sengbian ordered Qi to go to his relief; Chen Wudi also came from Ouyang to join him.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Qi general Guo Yuanjian attacked Yan Chaoda, Inspector of Qin Prefecture, at Qin Commandery. Wang Sengbian sent Qi to relieve him, and Chen Wudi came from Ouyang to join the fight.

sentences.zh: 元建眾卻，崱因縱兵大破之，元建遁。

translations.literal: Yuanjian's host withdrew; Qi thereupon loosed his troops and utterly defeated them, and Yuanjian fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjian's force withdrew. Qi pursued and routed them, and Yuanjian fled.

sentences.zh: 時元帝執王琳於江陵，琳長史陸納等於長沙反。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yuan held Wang Lin prisoner at Jiangling; Lin's Chief Clerk Lu Na and others rebelled at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Yuan held Wang Lin prisoner at Jiangling while Lin's chief clerk Lu Na rebelled at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 元帝征崱與王僧辯討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan summoned Qi and Wang Sengbian to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan sent Qi and Wang Sengbian against them.

sentences.zh: 及納等戰於車輪，大敗之。

translations.literal: When they fought Na and the others at Chelun, they utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: They met Na at Chelun and routed him.

sentences.zh: 後納等降，崱又與王僧辯西討平武陵王於硤口。

translations.literal: Later, when Na and the others surrendered, Qi again joined Wang Sengbian in the western campaign to pacify the Prince of Wuling at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: After Na surrendered, Qi joined Wang Sengbian in the western campaign that pacified the Prince of Wuling at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 旋鎮遘疾卒，諡曰武。

translations.literal: Soon after returning to his commandery he fell ill and died; his posthumous title was Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill on his post and died. His posthumous title was Martial.

sentences.zh: 崱兄弟九人，兄嵩、岑、嶷、岌、巘、岸及弟嵷、幼安並知名。

translations.literal: Qi had nine brothers: his elder brothers Song, Cen, Niao, Ji, Yan, and An, and his younger brothers Song and You'an—all were well known.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had nine brothers: Song, Cen, Niao, Ji, Yan, and An were his elders; Song and You'an were his younger brothers. All were well known.

sentences.zh: 岸字公衡，太清中，與崱隨岳陽王察攻荊州，同歸元帝。

translations.literal: An, style name Gongheng, in Taiqing followed Qi in accompanying the Prince of Yueyang Cha in attacking Jingzhou and returned together to Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: An, style name Gongheng, followed Qi in Taiqing when the Prince of Yueyang Cha attacked Jingzhou, then returned with him to Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 帝以為北梁州刺史，封江陵縣侯。

translations.literal: The emperor made him Inspector of Northern Liangzhou and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jiangling County.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him Inspector of Northern Liang Prefecture and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 岸請以五百騎襲襄陽，去城三十里，城中覺之。

translations.literal: An requested five hundred horsemen to strike Xiangyang; thirty li from the city, the city detected them.
translations.idiomatic: An asked for five hundred horsemen to strike Xiangyang. Thirty li from the city the garrison detected them.

sentences.zh: 察夜知其師掩襄陽，以岸等襄陽豪帥，於是夜遁歸襄陽。

translations.literal: Cha learned by night that his army was masking Xiangyang; because An and the others were powerful local leaders of Xiangyang, he thereupon fled by night back to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cha learned by night that his force was masking Xiangyang. Knowing An and the others were local magnates of Xiangyang, he fled back to the city that night.

sentences.zh: 岸等知察至，遂奔其兄南陽太守巘于廣平。

translations.literal: When An and the others learned that Cha had arrived, they fled to his elder brother Yan, Administrator of Nanyang, at Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When An and the others learned Cha had arrived, they fled to his brother Yan, Administrator of Nanyang, at Guangping.

sentences.zh: 察遣將尹正、薛暉等攻拔之，獲巘、岸等並其母妻子女，並斬於襄陽北門。

translations.literal: Cha sent generals Yin Zheng, Xue Hui, and others to attack and capture them; Yan, An, and the others, together with their mother, wives, sons, and daughters, were all beheaded at the north gate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cha sent Yin Zheng, Xue Hui, and others to take Guangping. Yan, An, their mother, wives, sons, and daughters were all beheaded at the north gate of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 察母龔保林數岸於眾，岸曰：「老婢教汝兒殺汝叔，乃枉殺忠良。」

translations.literal: Cha's mother, Lady Gong Baolin, reproached An before the crowd. An said: "Old slave, you taught your son to kill your own brother-in-law, yet you wrongly kill loyal men.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's mother Lady Gong Baolin denounced An before the crowd. An cried: "Old slave, you taught your son to kill his uncle, yet you butcher loyal men.

sentences.zh: 察命拔其舌，臠殺而烹之。

translations.literal: Cha ordered his tongue torn out, his flesh cut in strips, killed, and cooked.
translations.idiomatic: Cha ordered his tongue torn out, his flesh cut in strips, and him killed and cooked.

sentences.zh: 盡誅諸杜宗族親者，幼弱下蠶室，又發其墳墓，燒其骸骨，灰而揚之，並以為漆惋。

translations.literal: He put to death all of the Du clan and kin; the young and weak were sent to the silkworm chambers. He also opened their tombs, burned their bones, ground the ash and scattered it, and used it all for lacquer bowls.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the entire Du clan and kin. The young were castrated. He opened their tombs, burned the bones, ground the ash and scattered it, and made lacquer bowls from the remains.

sentences.zh: 及建鄴平，崱兄弟發安寧陵焚之，以報漆惋之酷，元帝亦不責也。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Qi's brothers opened the Anning Tomb and burned it to avenge the cruelty of the lacquer bowls; Emperor Yuan did not blame them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was pacified, Qi's brothers opened the Anning Tomb and burned it to avenge the lacquer-bowl outrage. Emperor Yuan did not reproach them.

sentences.zh: 幼安性至孝寬厚，雄勇過人，與兄崱同歸元帝，帝以為西荊州刺史，封華容縣侯。

translations.literal: You'an by nature was utmost in filial piety and generous breadth, with martial valor surpassing other men. He returned with his elder brother Qi to Emperor Yuan; the emperor made him Inspector of Western Jingzhou and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huarong County.
translations.idiomatic: You'an was deeply filial, generous, and surpassingly brave. He returned with Qi to Emperor Yuan, who made him Inspector of Western Jing Prefecture and Marquis of Huarong.

sentences.zh: 與王僧辯討河東王譽于長沙，平之。

translations.literal: He joined Wang Sengbian in suppressing the Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Wang Sengbian in suppressing the Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 又令助徐文盛東討侯景，至貝磯，大破景將任約，斬其儀同叱羅子通、湘州刺史趙威方等。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to assist Xu Wencheng in the eastern campaign against Hou Jing; reaching Beiji, he utterly defeated Jing's general Ren Yue and beheaded his Yitong Chiluo Zitong, Inspector of Xiangzhou Zhao Weifang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to aid Xu Wencheng against Hou Jing. At Beiji he routed Ren Yue and beheaded Chiluo Zitong, Zhao Weifang the Inspector of Xiang Prefecture, and others.

sentences.zh: 仍進軍大舉口，別攻拔武昌。

translations.literal: He then advanced to Dajukou and in a separate attack captured Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Dajukou and in a separate action took Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 景度蘆洲上流以壓文盛，幼安與眾軍大敗之。

translations.literal: Jing crossed upstream at Luzhou to press Wencheng; You'an, together with the armies, utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing crossed upstream at Luzhou to press Wencheng. You'an and the allied armies routed him.

sentences.zh: 會景密遣騎襲陷郢州，執刺史方諸，人情大駭，文盛由漢口遁歸，眾軍大敗，幼安降景，景以其多反復，殺之。

translations.literal: Just then Jing secretly sent cavalry by a hidden route to strike and capture Yingzhou, seizing Inspector Fang Zhu; morale was greatly shaken. Wencheng fled back by Hankou; the armies collapsed in great defeat. You'an surrendered to Jing; Jing killed him for his many shifts of allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing then sent cavalry by a hidden route and seized Ying Prefecture, capturing Inspector Fang Zhu. Panic spread. Wencheng fled up the Han, the armies broke, and You'an surrendered to Hou Jing, who killed him for his repeated betrayals.

sentences.zh: 龕，岑之子也，少驍勇，善用兵，與諸父歸元帝，帝以為鄖州刺史，封中廬縣侯，與王僧辯討平河東王譽。

translations.literal: Kan was Cen's son. From youth he was fierce and brave and skilled in using troops. He returned with his uncles to Emperor Yuan; the emperor made him Inspector of Yunzhou, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhonglu County, and he joined Wang Sengbian in pacifying the Prince of Hedong Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was Cen's son. From youth he was fierce, brave, and skilled in war. He returned with his uncles to Emperor Yuan, who made him Inspector of Yun Prefecture and Marquis of Zhonglu and sent him with Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Hedong Yu.

sentences.zh: 又隨僧辯下，繼徐文盛軍至巴陵。

translations.literal: He again followed Sengbian downstream, succeeding Xu's army and reaching Baling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Sengbian downstream, took over Xu's force, and reached Baling.

sentences.zh: 聞侯景陷郢州西上將至，乃與僧辯等守巴陵。

translations.literal: Hearing that Hou Jing had taken Yingzhou and was coming west upriver, he joined Sengbian and others in defending Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Hou Jing had taken Ying Prefecture and was marching upriver, he joined Sengbian in holding Baling.

sentences.zh: 景至圍之數旬，不克而遁。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived he besieged it for several tens of days, could not take it, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing besieged the city for weeks, failed to take it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷太府卿、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Palace Treasury and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of the Palace Treasury and Inspector of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及眾軍至姑孰，景將侯子鑒逆戰，龕與陳武帝、王琳等擊之，大敗子鑒，遂至石頭。

translations.literal: When the armies reached Gudu, Jing's general Hou Zijian met them in battle; Kan, together with Chen Wudi, Wang Lin, and others, struck him and utterly defeated Zijian, then reached Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies reached Gudu, Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian met them in battle. Kan, Chen Wudi, Wang Lin, and others routed Zijian and pressed on to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 景親會戰，龕與眾軍大破之。

translations.literal: Jing personally joined the battle; Kan and the armies utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing fought in person. Kan and the allied armies crushed him.

sentences.zh: 論功為最，授東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he ranked first and was appointed Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His merit ranked first, and he was made Inspector of Eastern Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又與王僧辯降陸納，平武陵王。

translations.literal: He again joined Wang Sengbian in receiving Lu Na's surrender and pacifying the Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Wang Sengbian in accepting Lu Na's surrender and pacifying the Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 及魏平江陵，後齊納貞陽侯明以紹梁嗣，以龕為震州刺史、吳興太守，遷南豫州刺史，封溧陽縣侯，又加散騎常侍、鎮南大將軍。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jiangling, Qi later received the Marquis of Zhenyang Ming to continue the Liang succession; Kan was made Inspector of Zhenzhou and Administrator of Wuxing, transferred to Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Liyang County, and further given Attendant Cavalry Regular and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei took Jiangling, Qi later installed the Marquis of Zhenyang Ming as heir to Liang. Kan became Inspector of Zhen Prefecture and Administrator of Wuxing, then Inspector of Southern Yu Prefecture and Marquis of Liyang, with added rank as Attendant Cavalry Regular and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 龕，僧辯婿也，始為吳興太守，以陳武帝既非素貴，及為之本郡，以法繩其宗門，無所縱舍。

translations.literal: Kan was Sengbian's son-in-law. When he first became Administrator of Wuxing, because Chen Wudi had not originally been of noble standing, and now that he was in his home commandery, Kan bound his clan by law without any indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was Sengbian's son-in-law. As Administrator of Wuxing he treated Chen Wudi, who had not been born to high rank, with strict law when Wudi returned to his home commandery, showing his clan no favor.

sentences.zh: 武帝銜之切齒。

translations.literal: Wudi bore a grudge against him to the grinding of teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi nursed a grudge that cut to the bone.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯敗，龕乃據吳興以拒之，頻敗陳文帝軍。

translations.literal: When Sengbian was defeated, Kan thereupon held Wuxing to resist him and repeatedly defeated Chen Wendi's armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian fell, Kan held Wuxing against the Chen and repeatedly defeated Wendi's armies.

sentences.zh: 龕好飲酒，終日恒醉，勇而無略，部將杜泰私通于文帝，說龕降文帝，龕然之。

translations.literal: Kan loved wine and was drunk all day long; he was brave but without strategy. His officer Du Tai secretly communicated with Wendi and urged Kan to surrender to Wendi; Kan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Kan drank constantly and was drunk all day. He was brave but lacked strategy. His officer Du Tai secretly contacted Wendi and urged surrender. Kan agreed.

sentences.zh: 其妻王氏曰：「霸先讎隙如此，何可求和。」

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Wang, said: "Baxian's enmity is so deep—how can we seek peace?
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Wang said: "Baxian's hatred runs so deep. How can we sue for peace?

sentences.zh: 因出私財賞募，復大敗文帝軍。

translations.literal: She thereupon brought out private wealth to reward recruitment and again utterly defeated Wendi's armies.
translations.idiomatic: She spent her private wealth to reward recruits and again routed Wendi's armies.

sentences.zh: 後杜泰降文帝，龕尚醉不覺，文帝遣人負出項王寺前斬之。

translations.literal: Later Du Tai surrendered to Wendi; Kan was still drunk and unaware. Wendi sent men to carry him out before Xiangwang Temple and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Du Tai surrendered to Wendi. Kan was still drunk and knew nothing until men carried him out before Xiangwang Temple and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 王氏因截發出家，杜氏一門覆矣。

translations.literal: The Lady Wang thereupon cut her hair and became a nun; the whole Du house was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang cut her hair and became a nun. The house of Du was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 王琳字子珩，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Wang Lin, style name Zihang, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin, style name Zihang, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 本兵家。

translations.literal: His family were originally military men.
translations.idiomatic: His family came from the military class.

sentences.zh: 元帝居蕃，琳姊妹併入後庭見幸，琳由此未弱冠得在左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan resided in his princely fief, Lin's sisters together entered the rear apartments and gained favor; Lin thereby, before his capping year, was able to remain at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan was still a prince, Lin's sisters entered the inner quarters and won favor. Lin therefore gained access to the prince before he came of age.

sentences.zh: 少好武，遂為將帥。

translations.literal: From youth he loved martial affairs and thereupon became a commander.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved arms and became a commander.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，帝遣琳獻米萬石，未至，都城陷，乃中江沈米，輕舸還荊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing the emperor sent Lin to present ten thousand shi of grain; before he arrived, the capital fell. He thereupon sank the grain mid-river and returned to Jing in light boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing the emperor sent Lin with ten thousand shi of grain. Before he arrived the capital fell. He sank the grain mid-river and returned to Jing in light boats.

sentences.zh: 稍遷岳陽內史，以軍功封建甯縣侯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Interior Minister of Yueyang and, for military merit, enfeoffed as Marquis of Ning County.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Interior Minister of Yueyang and, for military merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ning.

sentences.zh: 侯景遣將宋子仙據郢州，琳攻克之，禽子仙。

translations.literal: Hou Jing sent his general Song Zixian to hold Yingzhou; Lin captured it and took Zixian prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's general Song Zixian held Ying Prefecture. Lin took the city and captured Zixian.

sentences.zh: 又隨王僧辯破景。

translations.literal: He again followed Wang Sengbian in defeating Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Sengbian in defeating Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 後拜湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Inspector of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 琳果勁絕人，又能傾身下士，所得賞物不以入家，麾下萬人，多是江淮群盜。

translations.literal: Lin's fierceness and strength were unmatched among men; he could also throw himself down to honor subordinates. The rewards he received he did not bring into his household; under his command were ten thousand men, mostly river-bandits of the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's fierceness was unmatched, yet he humbled himself before his men. He never brought booty home. Ten thousand followers served him, mostly river bandits of the Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 平景之勳，與杜龕俱為第一。

translations.literal: In merit for pacifying Jing, he and Du Kan together ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In merit for pacifying Hou Jing he and Du Kan ranked first.

sentences.zh: 恃寵縱暴於建鄴，王僧辯禁之不可，懼將為亂，啟請誅之。

translations.literal: Relying on favor, he ran wild in Jiankang; Wang Sengbian could not restrain him and, fearing he would bring rebellion, memorialized requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on imperial favor he ran wild in Jiankang. Wang Sengbian could not restrain him and, fearing revolt, asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 琳亦疑禍，令長史陸納率部曲前赴湘州，身輕上江陵陳謝。

translations.literal: Lin also suspected disaster and ordered his Chief Clerk Lu Na to lead his troops ahead to Xiangzhou while he himself went lightly upriver to Jiangling to offer explanations.
translations.idiomatic: Lin also feared disaster. He sent his chief clerk Lu Na ahead to Xiang Prefecture with the troops while he went lightly to Jiangling to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 將行謂納等曰：「吾若不反，子將安之？」

translations.literal: As he was about to depart he said to Na and the others: "If I do not return, where will you settle?
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave he said to Na and the others: "If I do not return, where will you go?

sentences.zh: 咸曰：「請死」。

translations.literal: They all said: "We ask to die."
translations.idiomatic: They all said: "We ask only to die."

sentences.zh: 相泣而別。

translations.literal: They wept facing one another and parted.
translations.idiomatic: They wept and parted.

sentences.zh: 及至，帝以下吏，而使廷尉卿黃羅漢、太舟卿張載宣喻琳軍。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor handed him over to the law officers and sent Court Commandant Huang Luohan and Grand Boat Master Zhang Zai to proclaim the imperial will to Lin's army.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived the emperor handed him to the law officers and sent Court Commandant Huang Luohan and Grand Boat Master Zhang Zai to proclaim the imperial will to Lin's army.

sentences.zh: 陸納等及軍人並哭對使者，莫肯受命。

translations.literal: Lu Na and the others, together with the soldiers, all wept facing the envoys and would not accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na and the soldiers wept before the envoys and refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 乃縶黃羅漢，殺張載。

translations.literal: They thereupon bound Huang Luohan and killed Zhang Zai.
translations.idiomatic: They bound Huang Luohan and killed Zhang Zai.

sentences.zh: 載性刻，為帝所信，荊州疾之如讎，故納等因人之欲，抽其腸系馬腳，使繞而走，腸盡氣絕，又臠割備五刑而斬之。

translations.literal: Zai by nature was harsh and was trusted by the emperor; Jingzhou hated him like a foe. Therefore Na and the others, following men's desires, drew out his intestines, tied them to a horse's leg, and made him run in a circle until his entrails were exhausted and his breath ended; they then cut his flesh in strips, applied all five punishments, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was harsh and trusted by the emperor. Jingzhou hated him like an enemy. Na and the others drew out his intestines, tied them to a horse's leg, and made him run until he died. They then cut his flesh, applied the five punishments, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 元帝遣王僧辯討納，納等敗走長沙。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan sent Wang Sengbian to suppress Na; Na and the others were defeated and fled to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan sent Wang Sengbian against Na. Na was beaten and fled to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 是時湘州未平，武陵王兵下又甚盛，江陵公私恐懼，人有異圖。

translations.literal: At that time Xiangzhou was not yet pacified; the Prince of Wuling's armies descending were again very strong; public and private circles in Jiangling were afraid, and men harbored other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Prefecture was not yet pacified, the Prince of Wuling's armies were strong, and fear spread through Jiangling as men plotted.

sentences.zh: 納啟申琳無罪，請復本位，求為奴婢。

translations.literal: Na memorialized stating that Lin was without guilt, requesting restoration to his original post and asking to become slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Na memorialized that Lin was innocent, asked that he be restored to office, and offered to become slaves themselves.

sentences.zh: 元帝乃鎖琳送僧辯。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan thereupon chained Lin and sent him to Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan chained Lin and sent him to Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 時納出兵方戰，會琳至，僧辯升諸樓車以示之。

translations.literal: At that time Na had led his troops out and battle was underway; when Lin arrived, Sengbian mounted a tower carriage to show him to them.
translations.idiomatic: Na had led his troops out to fight. When Lin arrived, Sengbian mounted a tower carriage to show him to the army.

sentences.zh: 納等投戈俱拜，舉軍皆哭，曰：「乞王郎入城即出。」

translations.literal: Na and the others cast down their weapons and all bowed; the whole army wept and said: "We beg that Lord Wang enter the city, and we shall come out at once.
translations.idiomatic: Na and the others cast down their weapons and bowed. The whole army wept and cried: "Let Lord Wang enter the city and we shall come out at once.

sentences.zh: 乃放琳入，納等乃降。

translations.literal: They thereupon let Lin enter, and Na and the others then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They let Lin enter, and Na and the others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 湘州平，仍復琳本位，使拒武陵王紀。

translations.literal: When Xiangzhou was pacified, Lin was restored to his original post and ordered to resist the Prince of Wuling Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Prefecture was pacified, Lin was restored to his former post and ordered to resist the Prince of Wuling Ji.

sentences.zh: 紀平，授衡州刺史。

translations.literal: When Ji was pacified, he was appointed Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was pacified, he was made Inspector of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元帝性多忌，以琳所部甚盛，又得眾心，故出之嶺外。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan by nature was much given to suspicion; because Lin's command was very large and he also won the hearts of the masses, he was sent out beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was deeply suspicious. Because Lin's command was large and he won the hearts of his men, the emperor sent him beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 又授都督、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Commander and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Commander and Inspector of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其友人主書李膺，帝所任遇，琳告之曰：「琳蒙拔擢，常欲畢命以報國恩。

translations.literal: His friend Master of Documents Li Ying, whom the emperor favored and employed, Lin told him: "Lin has received elevation and always wished to exhaust his life in repaying the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Li Ying, Master of Documents, enjoyed the emperor's trust. Lin told him: "I have been raised up and have always wished to spend my life repaying the state's grace.

sentences.zh: 今天下未平，遷琳嶺外，如有萬一不虞，安得琳力。

translations.literal: The realm is not yet pacified, yet Lin is transferred beyond the mountains. If there should be any unforeseen trouble, how can Lin's strength be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not yet pacified, yet I am sent beyond the mountains. If trouble comes, how will my strength be available?

sentences.zh: 忖官正疑琳耳，琳分望有限，可得與官爭為帝乎？

translations.literal: I reckon the court suspects Lin; Lin's share of ambition is limited—how could he contend with the throne for empire?
translations.idiomatic: I reckon the court suspects me. My ambitions are limited. How could I contend with the throne for the empire?

sentences.zh: 何不以琳為雍州刺史，使鎮武寧。

translations.literal: Why not make Lin Inspector of Yongzhou and have him garrison Wuning?
translations.idiomatic: Why not make me Inspector of Yong Prefecture and have me garrison Wuning?

sentences.zh: 琳自放兵作田，為國禦捍，若警急動靜相知。

translations.literal: Lin would himself release troops to farm the fields and guard the state on its behalf; if alarm comes, movements can be known to one another.
translations.idiomatic: I would release the troops to farm and guard the frontier. If alarm comes, we can act in concert.

sentences.zh: 孰若遠棄嶺南，相去萬里，一日有變，將欲如何！

translations.literal: How does that compare with casting one far into the southern mountains, separated by ten thousand li—if change comes in a day, what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: How does that compare with casting me far into the southern mountains, ten thousand li away? If change comes in a day, what then?

sentences.zh: 琳非願長坐荊南，政以國計如此耳。」

translations.literal: Lin does not wish to sit long in southern Jing; it is only that the state's plan is thus.
translations.idiomatic: I do not wish to remain long in southern Jing. I act only as the state's plan requires.

sentences.zh: 膺然其言而不敢啟，故遂率其眾鎮嶺南。

translations.literal: Ying approved his words but did not dare report them; therefore Lin led his host to garrison the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Ying agreed but did not dare report it. Lin therefore led his host to garrison the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 元帝為魏圍逼，乃征琳赴援，除湘州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was pressed by Wei, he summoned Lin to relieve him and appointed him Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan was besieged by Wei, he summoned Lin to relieve him and made him Inspector of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 琳師次長沙，知魏平江陵，已立梁王察，乃為元帝舉哀，三軍縞素。

translations.literal: Lin's army halted at Changsha; learning that Wei had pacified Jiangling and established Prince Cha of Liang, he thereupon mourned for Emperor Yuan; the whole army wore white.
translations.idiomatic: Lin halted at Changsha. Learning that Wei had taken Jiangling and installed Prince Cha of Liang, he mourned Emperor Yuan and the whole army wore mourning white.

sentences.zh: 遣別將侯平率舟師攻梁，琳屯兵長沙，傳檄諸方，為進趣之計。

translations.literal: He sent a separate commander Hou Ping with river forces to attack Liang; Lin encamped at Changsha and issued proclamations to all quarters as plans for advance.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hou Ping with a fleet against Liang while he encamped at Changsha and issued proclamations for a general advance.

sentences.zh: 時長沙蕃王蕭韶及上游諸將推琳主盟。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Changsha Fan Xiao of the upper Yangzi and the generals there pushed Lin as alliance leader.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changsha Fan Xiao and the upstream generals made Lin leader of the alliance.

sentences.zh: 侯平雖不能度江，頻破梁軍。

translations.literal: Although Ping could not cross the Yangzi, he repeatedly defeated Liang armies.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ping could not cross the Yangzi, he repeatedly defeated Liang armies.

sentences.zh: 又以琳兵威不接，翻更不受指麾，琳遣將討之，不克。

translations.literal: Also, because Lin's military might did not connect with him, he in turn would no longer accept his command; Lin sent generals to suppress him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lin's power did not reach him, Ping refused his orders. Lin sent generals against him but failed.

sentences.zh: 又師老兵疲不能進，乃遣使奉表詣齊，並獻馴象；

translations.literal: Also, his army was old and weary and could not advance; he thereupon sent envoys with a memorial to Qi and presented tame elephants;
translations.idiomatic: His army grew old and weary and could not advance. He sent envoys to Qi with a memorial and presented tame elephants;

sentences.zh: 又使獻款于魏求其妻子；

translations.literal: he also sent pledges of submission to Wei to seek his wife and children;
translations.idiomatic: he also sent pledges to Wei seeking the return of his wife and children;

sentences.zh: 亦稱臣于梁。

translations.literal: he also declared himself a subject of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: he also declared himself a subject of Liang.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝既殺王僧辯，推立敬帝，以侍中、司空征琳。

translations.literal: After Chen Wudi killed Wang Sengbian and raised Emperor Jing, he summoned Lin with the posts of Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Wudi killed Wang Sengbian and raised Emperor Jing, he summoned Lin as Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 不從命，乃大營樓艦，將圖義舉。

translations.literal: Lin did not obey the command and thereupon built tower ships on a great scale, intending a righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: Lin refused and built tower ships on a great scale, intending a righteous rising.

sentences.zh: 琳將張平宅乘一艦，每將戰勝，艦則有聲如野豬，故琳戰艦以千數，以野豬為名。

translations.literal: Lin's general Zhang Ping's house had a single warship; whenever battle was about to be won, the ship would sound like a wild boar. Therefore Lin's battle ships numbered in the thousands and were named after wild boars.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's general Zhang Ping owned a warship that before victory would sound like a wild boar. Lin's fleet numbered in the thousands and was named the Wild Boars.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝遣將侯安都、周文育等討琳，仍受梁禪。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi sent generals Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyu, and others to suppress Lin; they still received Liang's abdication to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi sent Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyu, and others against Lin while accepting Liang's abdication to Chen.

sentences.zh: 安都歎曰：「我其敗乎，師無名矣。」

translations.literal: Andu sighed and said: "I am about to be defeated; the army has no righteous name.
translations.idiomatic: Andu sighed: "We are about to be defeated. The army fights without a righteous name.

sentences.zh: 逆戰於沌口。

translations.literal: They met in battle at Chun Kou.
translations.idiomatic: They met in battle at Chun Kou.

sentences.zh: 琳乘平肩輿，執鉞而麾之，禽安都、文育，其餘無所漏，唯以周鐵武一人背恩，斬之。

translations.literal: Lin rode in a level-shouldered carriage, held an axe, and directed them; he captured Andu and Wenyu, and of the rest not one escaped—only Zhou Tiewu alone had betrayed kindness, and he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Lin rode in an open carriage, held an axe, and directed the battle. He captured Andu and Wenyu without a single escape—only Zhou Tiewu, who had betrayed a kindness, was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 鎖安都、文育，置琳所坐艦中，令一閹豎監守之。

translations.literal: He chained Andu and Wenyu and placed them in the ship where Lin sat, with a eunuch to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: He chained Andu and Wenyu and placed them aboard his own ship under guard of a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 琳乃移湘州軍府就郢城，帶甲十萬，練兵於白水浦。

translations.literal: Lin thereupon moved the Xiangzhou military headquarters to Yingcheng, with one hundred thousand armored men drilling at Baishui Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the Xiangzhou headquarters to Yingcheng and drilled one hundred thousand armored men at Baishui Ford.

sentences.zh: 琳巡軍而言曰：「可以為勤王之師矣，溫太真何人哉！」

translations.literal: Lin reviewed the army and said: "They can serve as an army to rescue the throne—what sort of man was Wen Taizhen!
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the army he said: "This is an army fit to rescue the throne. What was Wen Taizhen compared to this?

sentences.zh: 南江渠帥熊曇朗、周迪懷貳，琳遣李孝欽、樊猛與余孝頃同討之。

translations.literal: The channel chieftains of the southern rivers Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di harbored double hearts; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoling together to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The southern river chieftains Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di wavered. Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoling against them.

sentences.zh: 三將軍敗，並為迪所囚。

translations.literal: The three generals were defeated and all were taken prisoner by Di.
translations.idiomatic: All three generals were defeated and imprisoned by Di.

sentences.zh: 安都、文育等盡逃還建鄴。

translations.literal: Andu, Wenyu, and the others all escaped back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Andu, Wenyu, and the others all escaped back to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 初，魏克江陵之時，永嘉王莊年甫七歲，逃匿人家。

translations.literal: Early on, when Wei captured Jiangling, the Prince of Yongjia Zhuang was only seven years old and hid in a common household.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling, the Prince of Yongjia Zhuang was only seven and hid among common people.

sentences.zh: 後琳迎還湘中，衛送東下。

translations.literal: Later Lin welcomed him back to Xiangzhong and escorted him east.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lin welcomed him back to the Xiang region and escorted him east.

sentences.zh: 及敬帝立，出質于齊，請納莊為梁主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing was established, he was sent as hostage to Qi, requesting that Zhuang be received as sovereign of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing was established, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi with a request that he be received as sovereign of Liang.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣遣兵援送，仍遣兼中書令李騊駼冊拜琳為梁丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi sent troops to escort him and also sent Acting Director of the Secretariat Li Taozhu to invest Lin as Liang's Chancellor, Commander of all armies at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi sent troops to escort Zhuang and dispatched Acting Director of the Secretariat Li Taozhu to invest Lin as Liang Chancellor, Commander of all armies, and Recorder of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 又遣中書舍人辛愨、遊詮之等齎璽書江表宣勞，自琳以下皆有頒賜。

translations.literal: He also sent Attendant of the Secretariat Xin Kai, You Quanzhi, and others with imperial seals to proclaim favor on the south of the Yangzi; from Lin downward all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Xin Kai, You Quanzhi, and others with imperial seals to proclaim favor south of the Yangzi. From Lin downward all received gifts.

sentences.zh: 琳乃遣兄子叔寶率所部十州刺史子弟赴鄴，奉莊纂梁祚於郢州。

translations.literal: Lin thereupon sent his elder brother's son Shubao to lead the sons of prefects of ten provinces under his command to Ye, to support Zhuang in assuming the Liang succession at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin sent his nephew Shubao with the sons of ten provincial governors to Ye to support Zhuang in assuming the Liang succession at Ying.

sentences.zh: 莊授琳侍中、使持節、大將軍、中書監，改封安成郡公，其餘並依齊朝前命。

translations.literal: Zhuang appointed Lin Palace Attendant, Commissioner with Full Credentials, Grand General, and Director of the Secretariat, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Ancheng Commandery; the rest followed Qi's earlier appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang made Lin Palace Attendant, Commissioner with Full Credentials, Grand General, and Director of the Secretariat, and changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Ancheng. The rest followed Qi's earlier appointments.

sentences.zh: 及陳文帝立，琳乃輔莊次於濡須口。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Chen was established, Lin thereupon supported Zhuang to camp second at Ruxu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Chen took the throne, Lin supported Zhuang in camp at Ruxu Ford.

sentences.zh: 齊遣揚州道行台慕容儼率眾臨江，為其聲援。

translations.literal: Qi sent the Yangzhou Branch Commander Murong Yan with his host to the river as vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Branch Commander Murong Yan of Yangzhou to the river as vocal support.

sentences.zh: 陳遣安州刺史吳明徹江中夜上，將襲盆城。

translations.literal: Chen sent Inspector of Anzhou Wu Mingche up the Yangzi by night, intending to strike Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent Wu Mingche, Inspector of An Prefecture, up the Yangzi by night to strike Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 琳遣巴陵太守任忠大敗之，明徹僅以身免。

translations.literal: Lin sent Administrator of Baling Ren Zhong to utterly defeat him; Mingche barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Lin sent Ren Zhong, Administrator of Baling, to rout him. Mingche barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 琳兵因東下，陳遣太尉侯瑱、司空侯安都等拒之。

translations.literal: Lin's army thereupon went east; Chen sent Grand Marshal Hou Tian, Minister of Works Hou Andu, and others to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's army marched east. Chen sent Grand Marshal Hou Tian and Hou Andu to resist.

sentences.zh: 瑱等以琳軍方盛，引軍入蕪湖避之。

translations.literal: Tian and the others, because Lin's army was at its height, drew their army into Wuhu to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lin's army was at its height, Tian withdrew into Wuhu to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 時西南風至急，琳謂得天道，將直取揚州，侯瑱等徐出蕪湖躡其後。
