translations.literal: At that time the southwest wind blew urgently; Lin thought he had obtained Heaven's way and intended to strike straight for Yangzhou; Hou Tian and the others slowly came out of Wuhu and followed his rear.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce southwest wind blew. Lin thought Heaven favored him and aimed straight at Yangzhou. Hou Tian slowly came out of Wuhu and followed his rear.

sentences.zh: 比及兵交，西南風翻為瑱用，琳兵放火燧以擲瑱船者，皆反燒其船。

translations.literal: When battle was joined, the southwest wind turned to Tian's use; Lin's army set fire beacons to hurl at Tian's ships, but all burned their own ships instead.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined the southwest wind turned to Tian's use. Lin's men hurled fire beacons at Tian's ships, but the flames burned their own fleet.

sentences.zh: 琳船艦潰亂，兵士透水死者十二三。

translations.literal: Lin's ships collapsed in disorder; soldiers who threw themselves into the water died twelve or thirteen in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's fleet collapsed. Twelve or thirteen in ten of his men who threw themselves into the water drowned.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆棄船上岸，為陳軍所殺殆盡。

translations.literal: The rest all abandoned their ships and went ashore and were killed by Chen's army almost to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: The rest abandoned ship and were killed on shore by Chen's army almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 初，琳命左長史袁泌、御史中丞劉仲威同典兵侍衛莊，及軍敗，泌遂降陳。

translations.literal: Early on, Lin had ordered his Left Chief Clerk Yuan Mi and Imperial Censor Liu Zhongwei together to command troops and attend Zhuang; when the army was defeated, Mi thereupon surrendered to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had ordered Yuan Mi and Liu Zhongwei to guard Zhuang. When the army was beaten, Mi surrendered to Chen.

sentences.zh: 仲威以莊投曆陽，又送壽陽。

translations.literal: Zhongwei took Zhuang to Liyang and again sent him to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei took Zhuang to Liyang and then to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 琳尋與莊同入齊，齊孝昭帝遣琳出合肥，鳩集義故，更圖進取。

translations.literal: Lin soon entered Qi together with Zhuang; Emperor Xiaozhao of Qi sent Lin out from Hefei to gather old adherents and plot anew.
translations.idiomatic: Lin soon entered Qi with Zhuang. Emperor Xiaozhao sent him out from Hefei to gather old adherents and plot anew.

sentences.zh: 琳乃繕艦，分遣招募淮南傖楚，皆願戮力。

translations.literal: Lin thereupon repaired ships and sent separate envoys to recruit the hired soldiers and Chu folk of Huainan; all wished to exert their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired ships and recruited hired soldiers and Chu folk of Huainan, who all wished to serve.

sentences.zh: 陳合州刺史裴景暉，琳兄瑉之婿也，請以私屬導引齊師，孝昭委琳與行台左丞盧潛率兵應赴。

translations.literal: Pei Jinghui, Inspector of He Prefecture under Chen and son-in-law to Lin's elder brother Min, requested to guide Qi troops with his private following; Xiaozhao entrusted Lin and Branch Commander Left Vice Director Lu Qian to lead troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jinghui, Chen's Inspector of He Prefecture and son-in-law to Lin's brother Min, offered to guide Qi troops with his private following. Xiaozhao entrusted Lin and Lu Qian to lead troops in response.

sentences.zh: 沈吟不決，景暉懼事泄，挺身歸齊。

translations.literal: He hesitated and could not decide; Jinghui feared the affair would leak out and threw himself on Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lin hesitated. Jinghui feared exposure and fled to Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊孝昭賜琳璽書令鎮壽陽，其部下將帥悉聽以從，乃除琳驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史，封會稽郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao granted Lin an imperial letter ordering him to garrison Shouyang; his officers and generals below were all permitted to follow, and he was further made Rapid Cavalry General, Bountiful Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Yangzhou, and Duke of Kuaiji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhao granted Lin an imperial letter ordering him to garrison Shouyang. His officers were permitted to follow. He was made Rapid Cavalry General, Bountiful Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Yang Prefecture, and Duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 又增兵秩，兼給鐃吹。

translations.literal: His military stipend was also increased, and drum-and-pipe music was added.
translations.idiomatic: His military stipend was increased and drum-and-pipe music was added.

sentences.zh: 琳水陸戒嚴，將觀釁而動，屬陳氏結好于齊，使琳更聽後圖。

translations.literal: Lin guarded strictly on land and water, intending to watch for an opening and act; because Chen made peace with Qi, Lin was made to wait for later plans.
translations.idiomatic: Lin guarded land and water, watching for an opening. Because Chen made peace with Qi, he was told to wait.

sentences.zh: 琳在壽陽，與行台尚書盧潛不協，更相是非，被召還鄴。

translations.literal: At Shouyang, Lin and Branch Commander Director of the Secretariat Lu Qian did not harmonize and slandered each other in turn; he was summoned back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouyang Lin quarreled with Lu Qian and was summoned back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊武成置而不問，除滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wucheng set the matter aside without inquiry and made him Inspector of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng set the matter aside and made him Inspector of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後以琳為特進、侍中。

translations.literal: Later Lin was made Special Palace Attendant and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Special Palace Attendant and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 所居屋脊無故剝破，出赤蛆數升，落地化為血，蠕動。

translations.literal: On the ridge of the house where he dwelt the tiles broke open without cause, and several sheng of red maggots emerged, fell to the ground, turned into blood, and writhed.
translations.idiomatic: The tiles on his house ridge broke open without cause. Several sheng of red maggots fell to the ground, turned to blood, and writhed.

sentences.zh: 有龍出於門外之池，雲霧起，晝晦。

translations.literal: A dragon appeared in the pool outside the gate; clouds and mist rose, and daylight grew dark.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon appeared in the pool outside his gate. Cloud and mist rose and daylight darkened.

sentences.zh: 會陳將吳明徹寇齊，齊帝敕領軍將軍尉破胡等出援秦州，令琳共為經略。

translations.literal: When Chen's general Wu Mingche invaded Qi, the Qi emperor ordered Commander of the Army Wei Pohu and others to go out to relieve Qinzhou and commanded Lin to share in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen's Wu Mingche invaded Qi, the Qi emperor ordered Wei Pohu and others to relieve Qin Prefecture and commanded Lin to share in the planning.

sentences.zh: 琳謂所親曰：「今太歲在東南，歲星居牛鬥分，太白已高，皆利為客，我將有喪。」

translations.literal: Lin said to those close to him: "Now the Grand Year is in the southeast, the Year Star in the Ox and Dipper division, and the White Planet already high—all favor the guest. I shall have a funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He told those close to him: "The Grand Year is in the southeast, the Year Star in the Ox and Dipper, the White Planet high—all favor the invader. I shall die.

sentences.zh: 又謂破胡曰：「吳兵甚銳，宜長策制之，慎勿輕鬥。」

translations.literal: He also said to Pohu: "Chen's troops are very sharp; long strategy should control them—do not fight lightly."
translations.idiomatic: He told Pohu: "Chen's troops are very sharp. Use long strategy. Do not fight lightly."

sentences.zh: 破胡不從。

translations.literal: Pohu would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Pohu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 戰，軍大敗。

translations.literal: In battle the army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In battle the army was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 琳單馬突圍，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Lin alone on horseback broke through the encirclement and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Lin alone broke through on horseback and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 還至彭城，齊令便赴壽陽，並許召募。

translations.literal: Returning to Pengcheng, Qi ordered him to go at once to Shouyang, and recruitment was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Pengcheng, Qi ordered him to go at once to Shouyang and permitted recruitment.

sentences.zh: 又進封琳巴陵郡王。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to Duke of Baling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was further advanced to Duke of Baling.

sentences.zh: 陳將吳明徹進兵圍之，堰肥水灌城。

translations.literal: Chen's general Wu Mingche advanced to besiege the city and dammed the Fei River to flood it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche advanced to besiege the city and dammed the Fei River to flood it.

sentences.zh: 而齊將皮景和等屯於淮西，竟不赴救。

translations.literal: Yet Qi's generals Pi Jinghe and others encamped west of the Huai and in the end did not go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi's Pi Jinghe and others camped west of the Huai and never came to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 明徹晝夜攻擊，城內水氣轉侵，人皆患腫，死病相枕。

translations.literal: Mingche attacked day and night; within the city moisture from the water spread, and all suffered swelling; the dead lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche attacked day and night. Moisture spread through the city, men swelled with disease, and the dead lay pillow to pillow.

sentences.zh: 從七月至十月，城陷被執，百姓泣而從之。

translations.literal: From the seventh month to the tenth the city fell and he was captured; the common people wept and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh month to the tenth the city fell and he was captured. The people wept and followed him.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹恐其為變，殺之城東北二十里，時年四十八。

translations.literal: Mingche feared he would cause trouble and killed him twenty li northeast of the city; he was forty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche feared trouble and killed him twenty li northeast of the city. He was forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 哭者聲如雷。

translations.literal: The sound of weeping was like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: The sound of weeping was like thunder.

sentences.zh: 有一叟以酒脯來至，號酹盡哀，收其血懷之而去。

translations.literal: An old man came with wine and dried meat, came to wail and pour libation with utmost grief, gathered his blood in his bosom, and went away.
translations.idiomatic: An old man came with wine and dried meat, wailed and poured libation, gathered Lin's blood in his bosom, and went away.

sentences.zh: 傳首建康，懸之於市。

translations.literal: His head was sent to Jiankang and hung in the market.
translations.idiomatic: His head was sent to Jiankang and hung in the market.

sentences.zh: 琳故吏梁驃騎府倉曹參軍朱瑒致書陳尚書僕射徐陵求琳首，曰：

translations.literal: Lin's former clerk Zhu Yang of the Rapid Cavalry Office wrote to Chen's Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Ling requesting Lin's head, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lin's former clerk Zhu Yang of the Rapid Cavalry Office wrote to Chen Vice Director Xu Ling requesting Lin's head, saying:

sentences.zh: 竊以朝市遷貿，時傳骨鯁之風；

translations.literal: I venture to observe that as the court and market shift, the age at times transmits the wind of firm backbone;
translations.idiomatic: I observe that as court and market shift, the age at times transmits the wind of firm backbone;

sentences.zh: 曆運推移，間表忠貞之跡。

translations.literal: as dynastic fortune moves, it at times displays the traces of loyal steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: as dynastic fortune moves, it at times displays the traces of loyal steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 故典午將滅，徐廣為晉家遺老；

translations.literal: Thus when Jin's dynasty was about to perish, Xu Guang became the Jin house's surviving elder;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Jin dynasty was about to perish, Xu Guang became the Jin house's surviving elder;

sentences.zh: 當塗已謝，馬孚稱魏室忠臣。

translations.literal: when the Dangtu regime had passed, Ma Fu was called a loyal minister of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: when the Dangtu regime had passed, Ma Fu was called a loyal minister of Wei.

sentences.zh: 用能播美於前書，垂名於後世。

translations.literal: By this means their beauty was spread in former books and their names handed down in later ages.
translations.idiomatic: By this means their fame was spread in former books and handed down in later ages.

sentences.zh: 梁故建寧公琳，洛濱餘胄，沂川舊族，立功代邸，效績中朝。

translations.literal: The late Duke of Jianning of Liang, Lin, was a remnant scion of the Luo banks, an old clan of the Yi River; he achieved merit at the substitute capital and rendered service in the central court.
translations.idiomatic: The late Duke of Jianning of Liang, Lin, was a remnant scion of the Luo banks, an old clan of the Yi River. He achieved merit at the substitute capital and served the central court.

sentences.zh: 當離亂之辰，總蕃伯之任。

translations.literal: In the season of division and chaos he bore overall the burden of the frontier lords.
translations.idiomatic: In the season of division and chaos he bore the burden of the frontier lords.

sentences.zh: 爾乃輕躬殉主，以身許國，實追蹤於往彥，信踵武于前修。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lightly gave his person to die for his lord and pledged his body to the state—truly he followed in the tracks of past worthies and surely trod in the martial footsteps of former cultivators.
translations.idiomatic: He lightly gave his person for his lord and pledged his body to the state, truly following past worthies and treading in the footsteps of former cultivators.

sentences.zh: 而天厭梁德，尚思匡繼，徒蘊包胥之念，終遘萇弘之眚。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven tired of Liang's virtue; he still thought to support and continue it, harboring only the thought of Shen Baoxu's plea, and in the end met the misfortune of Chang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven tired of Liang's virtue. He still thought to restore it, harboring Shen Baoxu's plea, and in the end met Chang Hong's fate.

sentences.zh: 洎王業光啟，鼎祚有歸，於是遠跡山東，寄命河北。

translations.literal: When the royal enterprise brightly opened and the tripod fortune had a return, he thereupon went far to the mountains east and entrusted his life to the lands north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal enterprise opened and the tripod fortune returned, he went far to the mountains east and entrusted his life north of the river.

sentences.zh: 雖輕旅臣之歎，猶懷客卿之禮。

translations.literal: Although he sighed the lament of a light-traveling minister, he still cherished the rites due a guest minister.
translations.idiomatic: Although he sighed the lament of a light-traveling minister, he still cherished the rites due a guest minister.

sentences.zh: 感茲知己，忘此捐軀。

translations.literal: Moved by such an understanding lord, he forgot this gift of his person.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by such a lord, he forgot the gift of his person.

sentences.zh: 至使身沒九泉，頭行萬里。

translations.literal: So that even when his person perished in the nine springs, his head traveled ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: So that even when his body perished in the nine springs, his head traveled ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 誠復馬革裹屍，遂其生平之志，原野暴骸，會彼人臣之節。

translations.literal: Truly again horse-hide may wrap the corpse and fulfill the ambition of his lifetime; exposed bones on the plain accord with the integrity of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Truly horse-hide may wrap the corpse and fulfill his life's ambition; exposed bones on the plain accord with a minister's integrity.

sentences.zh: 然身首異處，有足悲者。

translations.literal: Yet when body and head are in different places, there is ample cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when body and head lie in different places, there is ample cause for grief.

sentences.zh: 封樹靡卜，良可愴焉。

translations.literal: No grave mound could be chosen—truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: No grave could be chosen—truly pitiable.

sentences.zh: 瑒早簉末僚，預參下席，降薛君之吐握，荷魏公之知遇。

translations.literal: Yang early joined the lowest clerks, took part in the lower seats, received Lord Xue's grasp and release, and bore Duke Wei's knowing employment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang early served among the lowest clerks and shared the lower seats. He received Lord Xue's favor and Duke Wei's trust.

sentences.zh: 是用沾巾雨袂，痛可識之顏，回腸疾首，切猶生之面。

translations.literal: Therefore he wet his towel and rained his sleeves, grieved at a face once known, his entrails turning and his head aching, cut to the quick as though the face still lived.
translations.idiomatic: He wet his sleeves in grief for a face once known, his heart turning and his head aching as though Lin still lived.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖恩博厚，明詔爰發，赦王經之哭，許田橫之葬。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that sacred grace is broad and thick; a bright edict has been issued, pardoning Wang Jing's weeping and granting Tian Heng's burial.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before the court's broad grace. A bright edict has been issued, pardoning Wang Jing's weeping and granting Tian Heng's burial.

sentences.zh: 瑒雖芻賤，竊亦有心。

translations.literal: Though Yang is grass-low and mean, he secretly also has a heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yang is lowly, he too has a heart.

sentences.zh: 琳經蒞壽陽，頗存遺愛，曾游江右，非無舊德。

translations.literal: Lin once governed Shouyang and left much lingering kindness; he once traveled the lands west of the Yangzi and was not without old virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Lin once governed Shouyang and left kindness behind. He once traveled the lands west of the Yangzi and kept old ties.

sentences.zh: 比肩東合之吏，繼踵西園之賓，願歸彼境，還修窀穸。

translations.literal: Shoulder to shoulder with the clerks of the Eastern Pavilion, following in the footsteps of the guests of the Western Garden—I wish to return to that region and restore the burial mound.
translations.idiomatic: Side by side with Eastern Pavilion clerks, following Western Garden guests—I ask to return there and restore his burial.

sentences.zh: 庶孤墳既築，或飛銜土之燕，豐碑式樹，時留墮淚之人。

translations.literal: Perhaps when the lone tomb is built, swallows may fly bearing earth; when the rich stele is raised, men who shed tears may sometimes remain.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps when the lone tomb is built swallows will bear earth to it; when the rich stele is raised men will come to weep.

sentences.zh: 近故舊王綰等已有論牒，仰蒙制議，不遂所陳。

translations.literal: Recently old friends such as Wang Wan already submitted a petition; we looked up to receive imperial deliberation, yet what was stated was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Wang Wan and other old friends submitted a petition. We awaited imperial deliberation, but our request was denied.

sentences.zh: 昔廉公告逝，即肥川而建塋域，孫叔雲亡，仍芍陂而植楸檟。

translations.literal: Formerly when Lord Lian passed away, a grave domain was built at once on the Fei River; when Sun Shu died in the clouds, catalpa and oak were planted still at Quepi.
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Lian died a grave was built at once on the Fei River. When Sun Shu died, catalpa and oak were planted at Quepi.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，抑有其例。

translations.literal: From this speaking, there is indeed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see there is precedent.

sentences.zh: 不使壽春城下，唯傳報葛之人，滄洲島上，獨有悲田之客。

translations.literal: Do not let it be that below Shouchun city wall there is only the man who reported to Ge; on the islet of Cangzhou, only the guest who grieved for Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let Shouchun know only the man who reported to Ge, or Cangzhou only the guest who grieved for Tian.

sentences.zh: 昧死陳祈，伏待刑憲。

translations.literal: Risking death I state this prayer; I bow awaiting punishment by law.
translations.idiomatic: Risking death I state this prayer and bow awaiting the law.

sentences.zh: 陵嘉其志節，又明徹亦數夢琳求首，並為啟陳主而許之。

translations.literal: Ling admired his will and integrity; moreover Mingche also several times dreamed that Lin begged for his head—they all reported to the Chen ruler and he granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ling admired his integrity. Mingche too dreamed several times that Lin begged for his head. They reported to the Chen ruler and he granted it.

sentences.zh: 仍與開府主簿劉韶慧等持其首還于淮南，權瘞八公山側，義故會葬者數千人。

translations.literal: He then, together with Chief Clerk of the Bountiful Office Liu Shaohui and others, carried the head back to Huainan and provisionally buried it beside Mount Bagong; old adherents who came to the funeral numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He and Chief Clerk Liu Shaohui and others carried the head back to Huainan and provisionally buried it beside Mount Bagong. Several thousand old adherents attended the funeral.

sentences.zh: 瑒等乃間道北歸，別議迎接。

translations.literal: Yang and the others then returned north by hidden routes, separately planning a welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Yang and the others returned north by hidden routes to plan a welcome.

sentences.zh: 尋有揚州人茅智勝等五人密送喪柩達於鄴，贈十五州諸軍事、揚州刺史、侍中、特進、開府、錄尚書事，諡曰忠武王，葬給轀輬車。

translations.literal: Soon Yangzhou men Mao Zhisheng and five others secretly sent the coffin and reached Ye; he was posthumously granted Commander of military affairs of fifteen provinces, Inspector of Yangzhou, Palace Attendant, Special Palace Attendant, Bountiful Office, and Recorder of the Ministry of State Affairs, posthumous title Loyal Martial King, with a burial cart of the imperial procession given.
translations.idiomatic: Soon five men of Yangzhou including Mao Zhisheng secretly sent the coffin to Ye. He was posthumously granted Commander of fifteen provinces, Inspector of Yangzhou, Palace Attendant, Special Palace Attendant, Bountiful Office, and Recorder of the Ministry of State Affairs, with posthumous title Loyal Martial King and an imperial burial cart.

sentences.zh: 琳體貌閒雅，立發委地，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: Lin's bearing and appearance were refined and elegant; standing, his hair reached the ground; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was refined in bearing. Standing, his hair reached the ground. Joy and anger never showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 雖無學業，而強記內敏，軍府佐史千數，皆識其姓名。

translations.literal: Although without formal learning, he was strong in memory and inwardly keen; among the thousand-odd clerks of the military headquarters, he knew all their names.
translations.idiomatic: Though without formal schooling he had a powerful memory and inward keenness. Among a thousand headquarters clerks he knew every name.

sentences.zh: 刑罰不濫，輕財愛士，得將卒之心。

translations.literal: Punishments were not excessive; he prized wealth lightly and loved scholars, winning the hearts of commanders and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He did not punish excessively, prized wealth lightly, and loved his men, winning the hearts of officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 少為將帥，屢經喪亂，雅有忠義之節。

translations.literal: From youth a commander, he passed through many disorders and by nature possessed the integrity of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was a commander, passed through many disorders, and possessed loyal integrity by nature.

sentences.zh: 雖本圖不遂，齊人亦以此重之，待遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Although his original design was not fulfilled, the people of Qi also for this reason held him in weight and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Though his original design failed, Qi also respected him and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 及敗為陳軍所執，吳明徹欲全之，而其下將領多琳故吏，爭來致請，並相資給，明徹由此忌之，故及於難。

translations.literal: When defeated and captured by Chen's army, Wu Mingche wished to spare him, but many of the officers below were Lin's former clerks; they vied to come and plead, all aiding one another, and Mingche for this reason grew jealous of him—thus he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When captured by Chen, Wu Mingche wished to spare him, but many officers were Lin's old clerks and vied to aid him. Mingche grew jealous and thus he met disaster.

sentences.zh: 當時田夫野老，知與不知，莫不為之歔欷流泣。

translations.literal: At that time farmers and rustics, whether they knew him or not, all wept and shed tears for him.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers and rustics, whether they knew him or not, all wept for him.

sentences.zh: 觀其誠信感物，雖李將軍之恂恂善誘，殆無以加焉。

translations.literal: Observing how his sincerity and faith moved things, even General Li's gentle, good persuasion could hardly surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: His sincerity and faith moved all who met him. Even General Li's gentle persuasion could hardly surpass it.

sentences.zh: 琳十七子，長子敬在齊襲王爵，武平末通直常侍。

translations.literal: Lin had seventeen sons; the eldest son Jing in Qi inherited the princely rank and at the end of Wuping was Regular Attendant for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had seventeen sons. The eldest Jing inherited the princely rank in Qi and at the end of Wuping was Regular Attendant for Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 第九子衍，隋開皇中開府儀同三司，大業初，卒于渝州刺史。

translations.literal: The ninth son Yan, in Sui's Kaihuang era was Bountiful Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies; at the beginning of Daye he died as Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth son Yan in Sui's Kaihuang era held Bountiful Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies. Early in Daye he died as Inspector of Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張彪不知何許人，自雲家本襄陽，或云左衛將軍、衡州刺史蘭欽外弟也。

translations.literal: Zhang Biao—no one knew from where he came; he himself said his family was originally from Xiangyang, or it was said he was the younger brother-in-law of Left Guards General and Inspector of Hengzhou Lan Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao—no one knew his origin. He said his family was from Xiangyang, or that he was younger brother-in-law to Left Guards General and Inspector of Hengzhou Lan Qin.

sentences.zh: 少亡命在若邪山為盜，頗有部曲。

translations.literal: In youth he was an outlaw on Mount Ruoye as a bandit and had a considerable following.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was an outlaw bandit on Mount Ruoye with a considerable following.

sentences.zh: 臨城公大連出牧東揚州，彪率所領客焉。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Lincheng Dalian went out to govern Eastern Yangzhou, Biao led his followers to attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Lincheng Dalian governed Eastern Yang Prefecture, Biao brought his followers to serve him.

sentences.zh: 始為防合，後為中兵參軍，禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: He began as Defense Commander, later became Central Army Aide, and was treated with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Defense Commander and later became Central Army Aide, treated with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及侯景將宋子仙攻下東揚州，復為子仙所知。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing's general Song Zixian attacked and took Eastern Yangzhou, he again gained Zixian's recognition.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing's general Song Zixian took Eastern Yang Prefecture, Biao again won his recognition.

sentences.zh: 後去子仙，還入若邪舉義，征子仙不捷，仍走向剡。

translations.literal: Later he left Zixian, returned to Ruoye to raise a righteous force, campaigned against Zixian without success, and still fled toward Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left Zixian, returned to Ruoye to raise a righteous force, attacked Zixian without success, and fled toward Shan.

sentences.zh: 趙伯超兄子棱為侯景山陰令，去職從彪。

translations.literal: Zhao Bochao's elder brother's son Leng was Hou Jing's magistrate of Shanyin; he left office and followed Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bochao's nephew Leng had been Hou Jing's magistrate of Shanyin. He left office and followed Biao.

sentences.zh: 後懷異心，偽就彪計，請酒為盟，引刀子披心出血自歃，彪信之，亦取刀刺血報之。

translations.literal: Later he harbored a different heart, falsely joined Biao's plan, asked for wine to seal an oath, drew a knife, cut his chest open, and let blood flow to drink the oath himself; Biao believed him and also took a knife to stab blood in return.
translations.idiomatic: Later he harbored treachery, pretended to join Biao's plan, asked for wine to seal an oath, drew a knife, cut open his chest, and drank the blood. Biao believed him and stabbed his own blood in return.

sentences.zh: 刀始至心，棱便以手案之，望入彪心，刀斜傷得不深。

translations.literal: The knife had just reached the heart when Leng pressed it with his hand, aiming to enter Biao's heart; the knife slanted and the wound was not deep.
translations.idiomatic: The knife had just reached his heart when Leng pressed it aside toward Biao's heart. The blade slanted and the wound was not deep.

sentences.zh: 棱重取刀刺彪，頭面被傷頓絕。

translations.literal: Leng took the knife again and stabbed Biao; his head and face were wounded and he suddenly lost consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Leng stabbed Biao again. His head and face were wounded and he fell senseless.

sentences.zh: 棱謂已死，因出外告彪諸將，言已殺訖，欲與求富貴。

translations.literal: Leng thought him dead and went outside to tell Biao's generals that he had already killed him and wished to seek wealth and honor together.
translations.idiomatic: Leng thought him dead, went out to Biao's generals, said he had killed him, and asked to seek fortune together.

sentences.zh: 彪左右韓武入視，彪已蘇，細聲謂曰：「我尚活，可與手。」

translations.literal: Biao's attendant Han Wu entered to look; Biao had revived and in a low voice said to him: "I am still alive—you can lend a hand.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's attendant Han Wu looked in. Biao had revived and whispered: "I am still alive. Lend me a hand.

sentences.zh: 於是武遂誅棱。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu thereupon executed Leng.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wu executed Leng.

sentences.zh: 彪不死，復奉表元帝，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Biao did not die and again submitted a memorial to Emperor Yuan; the emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao survived and again memorialized Emperor Yuan, who greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 及侯景平，王僧辯遇之甚厚，引為爪牙，與杜龕相似，世謂之張、杜。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Wang Sengbian treated him very generously and drew him in as a claw—similar to Du Kan; the age called them Zhang and Du.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was pacified Wang Sengbian treated him generously as a trusted fighter, like Du Kan. The age called them Zhang and Du.

sentences.zh: 貞陽侯踐位，為東揚州刺史，並給鼓吹。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang ascended the throne, he was made Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou and given drum-and-pipe music as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Zhenyang took the throne, Biao was made Inspector of Eastern Yang Prefecture with drum-and-pipe music.

sentences.zh: 室富於財，晝夜樂聲不息。

translations.literal: His household was rich in wealth; music sounded day and night without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: His household was rich. Music sounded day and night without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 剡令王懷之不從，彪自征之。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Shan Wang Huaizhi would not obey; Biao campaigned against him himself.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Shan Wang Huaizhi would not obey. Biao marched against him himself.

sentences.zh: 留長史謝岐居守。

translations.literal: He left Chief Clerk Xie Qi to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: He left Chief Clerk Xie Qi to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 會僧辯見害，彪不自展拔。

translations.literal: When Sengbian was killed, Biao did not exert himself to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian was killed, Biao did not advance to help.

sentences.zh: 時陳文帝已據震澤，將及會稽，彪乃遣沈泰、吳寶真還州助岐保城。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Wendi already held Zhenze and was about to reach Kuaiji; Biao thereupon sent Shen Tai and Wu Baozhen back to the province to help Qi defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wendi already held Zhenze and was nearing Kuaiji. Biao sent Shen Tai and Wu Baozhen back to help Qi defend the city.

sentences.zh: 彪後至，泰等反與岐迎陳文帝入城。

translations.literal: Biao arrived later; Tai and the others in turn joined Qi in welcoming Chen Wendi into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Biao arrived later. Tai and the others turned and with Qi welcomed Wendi into the city.

sentences.zh: 彪因其未定，踰城而入。

translations.literal: Biao, because they were not yet settled, climbed over the wall and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Before they were settled Biao climbed the wall and entered.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝遂走出，彪復城守。

translations.literal: Chen Wendi thereupon fled out; Biao again defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi fled. Biao again held the city.

sentences.zh: 沈泰說陳文帝曰：「彪部曲家口並在香岩寺，可往收取。」

translations.literal: Shen Tai said to Chen Wendi: "Biao's followers' families are all at Xiangyan Temple—you can go and seize them."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tai told Wendi: "Biao's followers' families are all at Xiangyan Temple. You can go seize them."

sentences.zh: 遂往盡獲之。

translations.literal: He thereupon went and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: He went and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 彪將申進密與泰相知，因又叛彪，彪復敗走，不敢還城。

translations.literal: Biao's general Shen Jin was secretly in league with Tai; he therefore rebelled against Biao again. Biao was again defeated and fled, not daring to return to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's general Shen Jin was secretly in league with Tai and rebelled again. Biao was beaten and fled, not daring to return to the city.

sentences.zh: 據城之西山樓子，及暗得與弟昆侖、妻楊氏去。

translations.literal: He held the mountain tower on the western hills outside the city, and at dark was able to leave with his younger brother Kunlun and his wife the Lady Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He held a tower on the western hills outside the city and at dark left with his brother Kunlun and his wife Lady Yang.

sentences.zh: 猶左右數人追隨，彪疑之皆發遣，唯常所養一犬名黃蒼在彪前後，未曾舍離。

translations.literal: Still several men followed; Biao suspected them and sent them all away—only the dog he always kept, named Yellow Dark, was before and behind Biao and never left.
translations.idiomatic: Several men still followed. Biao suspected them and sent them all away. Only his dog Yellow Dark never left him.

sentences.zh: 乃還入若邪山中。

translations.literal: He thereupon returned into the mountains of Ruoye.
translations.idiomatic: He returned into the mountains of Ruoye.

sentences.zh: 沈泰說陳文帝遣章昭達領千兵重購之，並圖其妻。

translations.literal: Shen Tai urged Chen Wendi to send Zhang Zhaoda leading a thousand men with a heavy price on his head, and also to plot against his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tai urged Wendi to send Zhang Zhaoda with a thousand men and a heavy bounty, and to plot against his wife.

sentences.zh: 彪眠未覺，黃蒼驚吠劫來，便齧一人中喉即死。

translations.literal: Biao had not yet awakened from sleep when Yellow Dark barked in alarm at the robbers coming; he at once bit one man in the throat and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Biao slept. Yellow Dark barked at the robbers and bit one man in the throat, killing him.

sentences.zh: 彪拔刀逐之，映火識之，曰：「何忍舉惡。

translations.literal: Biao drew his sword to pursue them; by firelight he recognized them and said: "How can you bear to do evil.
translations.idiomatic: Biao drew his sword and by firelight recognized them. He said: "How can you bear to do evil?

sentences.zh: 卿須我者但可取頭，誓不生見陳蒨。」

translations.literal: If you need me, take only my head—I swear I will not live to see Chen Qian.
translations.idiomatic: If you need me, take only my head. I swear I will not live to see Chen Qian.

sentences.zh: 劫曰：「官不肯去，請就平地。」

translations.literal: The robbers said: "Your Lordship will not leave—please come to level ground."
translations.idiomatic: The robbers said: "You will not leave. Come to level ground."

sentences.zh: 彪知不免，謂妻楊呼為鄉里曰：「我不忍令鄉里落佗處，今當先殺鄉里然後就死。」

translations.literal: Biao knew he could not escape and said to his wife Yang, calling her "village mate": "I cannot bear to let the village mate fall into others' hands; now I must first kill the village mate and then go to death."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, he told his wife Yang, whom he called "village mate": "I cannot let my village mate fall into others' hands. I must kill her first, then die."

sentences.zh: 楊引頸受刀，曾不辭憚。

translations.literal: Yang stretched her neck to receive the blade and never showed fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yang stretched her neck to the blade without fear.

sentences.zh: 彪不下刀，便相隨下嶺到平處。

translations.literal: Biao would not bring down the blade and instead followed her down the ridge to level ground.
translations.idiomatic: Biao could not bring himself to strike and followed her down to level ground.

sentences.zh: 謂劫曰：「卿須我頭，我身不去也。」

translations.literal: He said to the robbers: "You need my head—my body will not leave.
translations.idiomatic: He told the robbers: "You need my head. My body will not leave.

sentences.zh: 呼妻與訣，曰：「生死從此而別，若見沈泰、申進等為語曰，功名未立，猶望鬼道相逢。」

translations.literal: He called his wife to farewell and said: "Life and death part here; if you see Shen Tai, Shen Jin, and the others, tell them for me: merit and fame are not yet established—we still hope to meet on the ghost road."
translations.idiomatic: He bade his wife farewell: "Life and death part here. If you see Shen Tai and Shen Jin, tell them merit is not yet won and we still hope to meet on the ghost road."

sentences.zh: 劫不能生得，遂殺彪並弟，致二首于昭達。

translations.literal: The robbers could not take him alive; they thereupon killed Biao and his brother and sent both heads to Zhaoda.
translations.idiomatic: The robbers could not take him alive. They killed Biao and his brother and sent both heads to Zhaoda.

sentences.zh: 黃蒼號叫彪屍側，宛轉血中，若有哀狀。

translations.literal: Yellow Dark howled beside Biao's corpse, rolling in the blood as though in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Dark howled beside Biao's corpse and rolled in the blood as though grieving.

sentences.zh: 昭達進軍，迎彪妻便拜，稱陳文帝教迎為家主。

translations.literal: Zhaoda advanced his army, went to meet Biao's wife and bowed, saying it was by Chen Wendi's order that he welcomed her as mistress of the house.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda advanced, met Biao's wife, and bowed, saying Wendi ordered him to welcome her as mistress of the house.

sentences.zh: 楊便改啼為笑，欣然意悅，請昭達殯彪喪。

translations.literal: Yang thereupon changed weeping to laughter, gladly pleased in mind, and asked Zhaoda to bury Biao's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Yang turned from weeping to laughter, pleased in mind, and asked Zhaoda to bury Biao.

sentences.zh: 墳塚既畢，黃蒼又俯伏塚間，號叫不肯離。

translations.literal: When the tomb mound was finished, Yellow Dark again lay prostrate among the graves, howling and refusing to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb was finished Yellow Dark lay among the graves, howling and refusing to leave.

sentences.zh: 楊還經彪宅，謂昭達曰：「婦人本在容貌，辛苦日久，請暫過宅莊飾。」

translations.literal: Yang passed Biao's house again and said to Zhaoda: "A woman's lot is in appearance; I have suffered long—please let me pass the house briefly to adorn myself.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Biao's house she told Zhaoda: "A woman's worth is in her face. I have suffered long. Let me pass the house briefly to adorn myself.

sentences.zh: 昭達許之。

translations.literal: Zhaoda granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda granted it.

sentences.zh: 楊入屋，便以刀割發毀面，哀哭慟絕，誓不更行。

translations.literal: Yang entered the house and thereupon used a knife to cut her hair and ruin her face, weeping in utmost grief and vowing never to go on.
translations.idiomatic: Yang entered, cut her hair, ruined her face, wept in utmost grief, and vowed never to go on.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝聞之，歎息不已，遂許為尼。

translations.literal: When Chen Wendi heard of it, he sighed without end and thereupon permitted her to become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi heard he sighed endlessly and permitted her to become a nun.

sentences.zh: 後陳武帝軍人求取之，楊投井決命。

translations.literal: Later Chen Wudi's soldiers came to take her; Yang threw herself into a well to end her life.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wudi's soldiers came for her. Yang threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 時寒，比出之垂死，積火溫燎乃蘇，復起投於火。

translations.literal: It was cold; when they pulled her out she was nearly dead; they heaped fire to warm her and she revived, then rose and threw herself into the fire again.
translations.idiomatic: It was cold. Pulled out she was nearly dead. They warmed her with fire and she revived, then threw herself into the fire again.

sentences.zh: 彪始起於若邪，興於若邪，終於若邪。

translations.literal: Biao first rose at Ruoye, flourished at Ruoye, and ended at Ruoye.
translations.idiomatic: Biao rose at Ruoye, flourished at Ruoye, and ended at Ruoye.

sentences.zh: 及妻犬皆為時所重異。

translations.literal: His wife and dog were both held strange and weighty by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and dog were both held in wonder by the age.

sentences.zh: 楊氏，天水人，散騎常侍曒之女也。

translations.literal: The Lady Yang was a native of Tianshui, daughter of Regular Attendant-at-Large Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was from Tianshui, daughter of Regular Attendant-at-Large Yang.

sentences.zh: 有容貌，先為河東裴仁林妻，因亂為彪所納。

translations.literal: She had beauty; she was first wife to Pei Renlin of Hedong and, because of disorder, was taken by Biao.
translations.idiomatic: She was beautiful, had first been wife to Pei Renlin of Hedong, and in the disorder was taken by Biao.

sentences.zh: 彪友人吳中陸山才嗟泰等翻背，刊吳昌門為詩一絕曰：「田橫感義士，韓王報主臣，若為留意氣，持寄禹川人。」

translations.literal: Biao's friend Lu Shancai of Wu in the middle lands lamented Tai and the others' betrayal and carved on Wu's Chang Gate a single quatrain: "Tian Heng moved righteous men; the King of Han repaid his lord's minister—if you would keep faith in spirit, hold it out to the man of Yuchuan."
translations.idiomatic: Biao's friend Lu Shancai of Wu lamented Tai's betrayal and carved on Chang Gate a quatrain: "Tian Heng moved righteous men; the King of Han repaid his lord's minister—if you would keep faith in spirit, hold it out to the man of Yuchuan."

sentences.zh: 論曰：忠義之道，安有常哉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The way of loyalty and righteousness—how can it have a constant rule?
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: The way of loyalty and righteousness—how can it have a constant rule?

sentences.zh: 善言者不必能行，蹈之者恒在所忽。

translations.literal: Those good at words are not necessarily able to act; those who tread the path are always in what is overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: Those good with words cannot always act. Those who walk the path are always overlooked.

sentences.zh: 江子一、胡僧佑，太清之季，名宦蓋微。

translations.literal: Jiang Ziyi and Hu Sengyou—in the Taiqing season their fame and office were slight.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ziyi and Hu Sengyou—in the Taiqing season their fame and office were slight.

sentences.zh: 江則自致亡軀，胡亦期之殞命，然則貞勁之節，歲寒自有性也。

translations.literal: Jiang brought destruction on his own person; Hu also expected to die—yet the integrity of firm steadfastness, in cold years, has its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang brought death on himself; Hu also expected to die—yet firm integrity has its nature in cold years.

sentences.zh: 文盛克終有鮮，詩人得所誡焉。

translations.literal: Wencheng could not keep his end clean—the poets found in him a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng could not keep his end clean—the poets found a warning in him.

sentences.zh: 子春戰乃先鳴，幽通有助，及乎梁州之敗，而以濯足為尤。

translations.literal: Zichun in battle was first to cry out; hidden communication had its help; yet when it came to Liangzhou's defeat, washing the feet was held a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Zichun was first to cry out in battle and had help from hidden powers—yet when Liang Prefecture fell, washing his feet was held against him.

sentences.zh: 杜氏終致覆亡，亦云圖墓之咎。

translations.literal: The Du house in the end was overthrown—it is also said this was the fault of plotting the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The Du house was destroyed in the end—some also say this was the fault of plotting the tomb.

sentences.zh: 吉凶之兆，二者豈易知乎。

translations.literal: Omens of fortune and misfortune—these two, are they easy to know?
translations.idiomatic: Omens of fortune and misfortune—are the two easy to know?

sentences.zh: 王琳亂朝忠節，志雪仇恥，然天方相陳，義難弘濟，斯則大廈落構，豈一木所能支也。

translations.literal: Wang Lin disturbed the court with loyal integrity and wished to avenge disgrace—yet Heaven was then favoring Chen; righteousness could hardly be broadly achieved. This is a great hall whose beams have fallen—how can a single timber support it?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin disturbed the court with loyal integrity and wished to avenge disgrace—yet Heaven favored Chen and righteousness could not prevail. When the great hall's beams fall, how can one timber support it?

sentences.zh: 張彪一遇何懷，死而後已；

translations.literal: Zhang Biao, once he met He Huai, died only afterward;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao, once he met He Huai, did not stop until death;

sentences.zh: 唯妻及犬，義悉感人，記傳所陳，何以加此，異乎！

translations.literal: only his wife and dog—all their righteousness moved men. What the records relate—how can one add to this? Strange indeed!
translations.idiomatic: only his wife and dog—all their righteousness moved men. What the records tell—how can one add to this? Strange indeed!
